**Stage F stopped before any Datadog-specific code, on a real, confirmed architectural gap found while surveying `sdk/providers/.ubx/config` for Datadog's own real entries** (not guessed, not assumed -- read directly): every real provider's schema is NOT one `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` entry -- it's a GROUP (`dynamic_provider_groups.<x>_all`, `repo_name` = the real published identity) merging multiple named entries, and a large fraction of those entries are `data_sources = true` (data-source mode, a structurally different discovery+translation pipeline from resource mode -- `resourcemap.BuildDataSources`/`smithy.BuildDataSources`/`discoverydoc.BuildDataSources`, not `dynserver.Build`/`smithy.Build`/`discoverydoc.Build`). Real counts, read directly from the live config:

| Group | repo_name | total members | data-source members |
|---|---|---|---|
| kubernetes_all | kubernetes | 2 | 1 (`kubernetes_ds`) |
| github_all | github | 2 | 1 (`github_ds`) |
| datadog_all | datadog | 4 | 2 (`datadog_ds`, `datadog_v2_ds`) |
| aws_data_all | aws | 430 | 429 (`aws_data_*`; only the CFN `aws` entry itself is resource-mode) |
| google_all | google | 524 | 262 |
| azure_all | azure | 604 | 302 |

**Confirmed directly against the real code, not inferred**: `internal/snapshot.Snapshot` has no field recording resource-vs-data-source mode at all. `GenerateOpenAPI` (pre-existing, unchanged by UBI-182) always calls `dynserver.Build` (resource discovery) -- never `resourcemap.BuildDataSources`, regardless of `cfg.DataSources`. `runServeSnapshot`'s openapi branch always builds `&dynserver.Server{Resources: resources, ...}` -- never `DataSources: ...`. This is a real, pre-existing gap in the ORIGINAL openapi-only snapshot mechanism (predates UBI-182), not something this session introduced for openapi -- but Stage A's own new `GenerateCloudFormation`/`GenerateSmithy`/`GenerateDiscoveryDoc` (this session's work) replicated the identical resource-only scope for the three new sources too, without closing the gap: `GenerateSmithy` always calls `smithy.Build`, never `smithy.BuildDataSources`, the same real asymmetry `run()`'s own live-fetch branch already handles correctly for AWS's real data sources today.

**Real consequence, not hypothetical**: a `[providers.<name>]`-pinned data-source-mode entry today would not fail loud -- it would silently serve RESOURCE-shaped schemas instead of data-source-shaped ones (or, for cloudformation/smithy/discoverydoc, `--generate-snapshot` would just be missing entirely for that mode). This means Kubernetes' own prior "Stage D complete end to end" entry was only half true: `[dynamic_providers.kubernetes]` (resource mode, `repo_name=kubernetes`'s smaller half) is genuinely pinned and verified; `kubernetes_ds` (the group's OTHER real member) was never attempted and would misbehave if pinned today under the current mechanism.

**Two real, separate open design questions, not decided here, reported instead of guessed at**:
1. Data-source-mode snapshot support: `Snapshot` needs a mode field (or equivalent), and all three of `GenerateOpenAPI`/`GenerateSmithy`/`GenerateDiscoveryDoc` (CloudFormation has no data-source concept, confirmed earlier this arc) plus `runServeSnapshot`/`--dump-signals`/`--dump-namespaces` need a real data-source branch mirroring `run()`'s own live-fetch logic -- a real, scoped `ubx-provider-dynamic` change, not small (touches every source but CFN).
2. Group-level identity: a provider's real published `ubx-schema-<name>` identity is the GROUP (`repo_name`), not any one member -- but the snapshot mechanism only knows how to generate/pin ONE entry at a time. Datadog alone needs 4 real per-entry snapshots (2 resource, 2 data-source) reconciled into ONE coherent, versioned, pinnable artifact; AWS needs 430. No existing mechanism merges multiple snapshots into one identity, or represents "this release covers members X, Y, Z" at all.

**Not done**: no `ubx-schema-datadog` repo created, no snapshot generated, no code written for Datadog. Stopped here deliberately -- proceeding would either produce an incomplete artifact (2 of 4 real members) or require inventing an unreviewed design for both gaps above, exactly the "surfaces once, not five times" case the founder asked to catch early.

**Real measurements taken to answer "does one merged snapshot per repo hold at AWS's 430-member scale," not estimated**: shallow-cloned the real `github.com/aws/api-models-aws` and measured the exact 429 files the config's own `aws_data_*` `schema_url`s point at (all 429 found, zero missing) -- **157.45 MB** raw JSON (min 18KB, median 238KB, max 6.66MB per service). Fetched and unzipped the real CloudFormation registry (`CloudformationSchema.zip`, 2.96MB compressed) -- **17MB** raw JSON across 1,720 files. Combined real raw content for the whole `aws` group: **~174.5MB**. Measured the real inflation `Snapshot.Save`'s own `json.MarshalIndent` + `RawSpec` re-encoding actually produces (Kubernetes' own already-published pair: 4,475,339 bytes fetched -> 5,809,082 bytes committed, a real **~1.30x** multiplier) -- applied to AWS's raw total: **~227MB** for one flat, uncompressed, merged `snapshot.json`.

**This exceeds GitHub's own real, hard per-file commit limit (100MB, no LFS) by more than 2x -- "one flat committed snapshot.json" does not hold at AWS's scale, confirmed, not assumed.** Compression tested for real: concatenated the real raw AWS content (179MB) and gzipped it -- **17.9MB**, a real ~10x ratio (highly repetitive, structured JSON compresses well). Comfortably under every real limit, but a compressed blob is not human-diffable, which directly conflicts with this design's own stated reason for committing the snapshot at all ("a reviewer sees the real diff on every version bump," docs/plan.md's UBI-182 changelog entry) -- solves the size problem, defeats the reviewability goal that motivated committing in the first place.

**Proposed design A -- group-level container, reported not built**: restructure the on-disk snapshot from one flat `RawSpec` into a container recording the group's own real identity (`Provider` = `repo_name`, one `Version` for the whole group) plus a `Members map[string]*MemberSnapshot`, each member keeping its OWN `SchemaSource`/`RawSpec`/mode/auth/etc -- this is what actually makes a mixed-source group representable at all (AWS's own `aws` group is NOT single-source: 1 CFN member + 429 Smithy members, a real blocker for "one Snapshot, one SchemaSource" as it exists today, confirmed against the struct directly). Generation stays per-member exactly as `--generate-snapshot` already works today (no group-awareness added to that flag) -- a new, separate, small merge step (proposed as a new `--generate-snapshot-group` mode, taking pre-generated per-member snapshot paths + a group's member list, no live network fetch of its own) assembles them into the container and derives ONE real version for the whole group by taking the max `ChangeLevel` across every member's own diff against the prior container's corresponding member. Runtime: each real member keeps its own `[providers.<member-name>]` pin (e.g. both `[providers.kubernetes]` and `[providers.kubernetes_ds]`), `source` pointing at the SAME repo/version for both -- `provider.AcquireSchema`'s own existing cache-by-source+version already deduplicates this into ONE real download/cache-write regardless of how many members reference it, with zero change needed to `AcquireSchema` itself; the launched subprocess picks its own member out of the container via `UBX_DYNAMIC_PROVIDER_NAME`, which it already receives.

**Committed-artifact shape, the one real remaining open question in design A, not decided here**: either (a) one compressed `snapshot.json.gz` (simple, small `AcquireSchema` change -- try the compressed asset name first, fall back to today's plain `snapshot.json` so Kubernetes' own already-published `v1.0.0` stays loadable unchanged -- but not reviewable in a real PR diff), or (b) commit each member as its own small, real, diffable JSON file under `members/<name>.json` plus a top-level `manifest.json`, and have the RELEASE step bundle them into one compressed archive asset for `AcquireSchema` to download/extract (reviewable AND small, but a real, bigger change to `AcquireSchema`'s own download/cache contract -- archive extraction, not a single-file write). Kubernetes (2 small members, ~5.8MB combined) doesn't need either mitigation and would work fine either way -- this choice only bites at real scale (AWS/google/azure), which is exactly why it's worth deciding before, not during, the AWS rollout.

**Proposed design B -- data-source mode, fail loud on mismatch, per the founder's own explicit requirement**: add a real `Mode` field (`resource` / `data_source`) to each `MemberSnapshot`. `GenerateOpenAPI`/`GenerateSmithy`/`GenerateDiscoveryDoc` each gain a mode-aware branch calling the already-real, already-used-by-`run()`'s-own-live-fetch-path `resourcemap.BuildDataSources(doc, providerName)` / `smithy.BuildDataSources(doc, providerName, svc, namespaceOverride)` / `discoverydoc.BuildDataSources(doc, providerName, versionQualifier)` instead of the resource-mode `Build` when `Mode == data_source` -- no new translation logic, reusing exactly what the live path already does correctly. CloudFormation has no data-source concept at all (confirmed directly: zero `BuildDataSources`/`DataSource` references anywhere in `internal/cloudformation`) -- `GenerateCloudFormation`/`LoadCloudFormation` refuse `Mode == data_source` with a real, explicit, named sentinel error, immediately, rather than silently building resource-shaped output under a data-source label. `runServeSnapshot`/`--dump-signals`/`--dump-namespaces` all gain the identical mode check before dispatch -- a snapshot whose own recorded `Mode` doesn't match what the caller/binary can actually serve for that `SchemaSource` fails loud, at the earliest possible point, never falls through to the wrong shape.

**What it takes to close `kubernetes_ds`, concretely -- the real, minimal proof of designs A+B, proposed as the next real work once approved**: Kubernetes is the ideal second pilot for the CONTAINER format specifically because it has exactly 2 members, both openapi, both fetched from the identical `schema_url` (no CFN+Smithy mixed-source complexity, no 430-member fetch/rate-limit operational cost) -- the smallest real proof that a container can hold one resource-mode member and one data-source-mode member correctly, before ever attempting AWS. Concrete steps: (1) build design A's container shape + `--generate-snapshot-group` merge step in `ubx-provider-dynamic`, (2) build design B's `Mode` field + `resourcemap.BuildDataSources` branch for openapi specifically (the other two sources' data-source branches can follow once needed, not required to unblock Kubernetes), (3) regenerate `ubx-schema-kubernetes` as a real 2-member container (a new version -- `v1.0.0`'s own existing format-2, single-member shape is superseded, not silently reinterpreted; whether to keep `v1.0.0` loadable via a compatibility shim in `Load` or accept the break given nothing but this session's own verification tests currently depends on it is a real, explicit sub-question for the founder, not decided here), (4) re-verify `[providers.kubernetes]` AND newly add `[providers.kubernetes_ds]`, both pinned against the same repo/version, both independently proven zero-network on a cache hit the same way `[providers.kubernetes]` alone already was, (5) only then is `repo_name = "kubernetes"`'s own real, whole group genuinely, completely pinned -- the actual bar "Stage D complete" should have been held to.

**Not built. Reported, per the founder's own explicit "report before building."**

**Founder answered both open questions directly, no further design ambiguity**: artifact shape is per-member files (`members/<name>.json`) plus a `manifest.json`, committed separately for real diffability, packed into one compressed archive only at release time (accepting the larger `AcquireSchema` change this implies). `v1.0.0`'s own format-2 shape gets no compatibility shim -- accepted break, republish Kubernetes as a real, breaking `v2.0.0` container. Build both designs, close `kubernetes_ds` as the second pilot, verify both members zero-network including the negative control.

**Design A (group container) and Design B (resource/data-source mode, fail loud) both built in full, in `ubx-provider-dynamic`**: `internal/snapshot.Snapshot` restructured into a real container (`Provider` = group repo identity, one `Version` for the whole group via `AssembleGroup` -- max real change level across every member, unconditional Major for any member that disappears entirely) holding a `Members map[string]*MemberSnapshot`, each keeping its own `SchemaSource`/`Mode`/`RawSpec`. `SchemaFormat` moved to 3 (Min and Max together -- the old format-2 shape is refused outright by the existing `CheckFormat` mechanism, no special-casing needed). Every `Generate<Source>Member`/`Load<Source>Member` (renamed from the old flat `Generate<Source>`/`Load<Source>`) is now `Mode`-aware: `ModeResource` calls the existing `Build` pipeline, `ModeDataSource` calls the real, already-used-by-`run()`'s-own-live-fetch-path data-source builders (`resourcemap.BuildDataSources`/`smithy.BuildDataSources`/`discoverydoc.BuildDataSources` -- no new translation logic). CloudFormation has no data-source concept at all (confirmed directly, zero references anywhere in `internal/cloudformation`) -- requesting `ModeDataSource` against it fails immediately with `ErrUnsupportedMode`, at both generate time and load time, the founder's own explicit "fail loudly, never fall through" requirement made real and tested (`TestGenerateCloudFormationMember_DataSourceMode_RealFailLoud`, `TestLoadCloudFormationMember_DataSourceMode_RealFailLoud`).

`--generate-snapshot` (single-member) replaced entirely by `--generate-snapshot-group` (`--group-repo-name`, `--group-members`, reused `--prev-snapshot`) -- reads every named `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` table from the SAME `.ubx/config` (`config.Load`, not `LoadNamed`), generates each real member, and assembles one real group container. `runServeSnapshot`/`--dump-signals`/`--dump-namespaces` all rewritten to load the container, resolve their own member by the `UBX_DYNAMIC_PROVIDER_NAME` they already receive (`Snapshot.Member`), and dispatch per that member's own real `SchemaSource`+`Mode`. New `SaveSplit`/`LoadSplit` write/read the real, committable directory shape (`manifest.json` + `members/<name>.json`, separately diffable) -- `Save`/`Load` (single-file) kept as a simpler primitive for hermetic tests, no longer used by any real CLI path. All new code covered by hermetic tests (mode dispatch, fail-loud refusal, `AssembleGroup`'s own version-derivation rules, `SaveSplit`/`LoadSplit` round trip). `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean whole-repo, gofmt clean.

**`provider.AcquireSchema` (ubiquex) updated to match -- archive download, not a single file**: release asset renamed `snapshot.json` -> `snapshot.tar.gz`; `AcquireSchemaResult.Path` is now a directory (the real extracted cache entry), `AcquireSchemaResult.SHA256` is the archive's own real digest, populated only for a fresh download (empty for a cache/mirror hit -- a directory has no one meaningful hash to report, and re-verifying an already-verified hit was never the point). **Founder question, before touching Datadog further**: pinning both `[providers.kubernetes]` and `[providers.kubernetes_ds]` means a user writes two config blocks for one real provider -- the resource/data-source split is an internal discovery-time detail, not something a user should need to know. The container format already holds both members in one snapshot. Does anything genuinely require two pins, or can one pin serve both? If nothing does, fix it before Stage F multiplies two blocks into twelve.

**Confirmed directly, not assumed: nothing in the wire protocol or this binary's own server types ever required two pins.** `tfprotov6.GetProviderSchemaResponse` (checked against the real dependency source, not just this codebase) carries `ResourceSchemas` and `DataSourceSchemas` as two independent map fields on the SAME response. `dynserver.Server` and `smithyserver.Server` already both carry `Resources` AND `DataSources` fields and already merge them into one response inside their own existing `GetProviderSchema` handlers (`cfnserver.Server` has no `DataSources` field at all, since CloudFormation genuinely has no data-source concept). The two-pin requirement was purely an artifact of `run()`'s own live-fetch branching (one config table, one bool, one launch) -- never a real constraint.

**Built in `ubx-provider-dynamic`, new file `internal/snapshot/mergegroup.go`**: `GroupSchemaSource` (verifies every member of a group shares one real `SchemaSource`, refuses loudly -- `ErrMixedSchemaSourceGroup` -- on a real mix, naming AWS's own CFN+Smithy group as the real, already-deferred case this exists for). `MergeOpenAPIGroup`/`MergeSmithyGroup`/`MergeDiscoveryDocGroup`/`MergeCloudFormationGroup` union every real member's own resources/data-sources into one server's worth of content, refusing loudly (`ErrDuplicateWireType`) on any real collision within the same schema role rather than letting Go's own map-merge order silently pick a winner. `ExecConfig` verifies every real member shares the same `BaseURL`/`Auth` before picking one to execute real CRUD with (`ErrInconsistentExecConfig` otherwise -- not hit by any real config today, a real, deliberate safety check). `runServeSnapshot`/`--dump-signals`/`--dump-namespaces` all rewritten: a pinned launch now requires its own `UBX_DYNAMIC_PROVIDER_NAME` to equal the snapshot's own real `Provider` identity (fails loud on a stray old-style sub-member reference like `kubernetes_ds`) and serves the WHOLE merged group.

**A real, connected bug found and fixed while building this, affecting already-published data**: `GenerateOpenAPIMember`/`LoadOpenAPIMember` never threaded `wire_name` through to translation at all -- always used the raw table key instead, silently ignoring the field entirely (unlike `GenerateSmithyMember`, which already did this correctly). `GenerateDiscoveryDocMember`/`LoadDiscoveryDocMember` had the identical gap for their own data-source mode specifically (resource mode correctly uses bare name, matching `run()`'s own real, documented asymmetry). Confirmed live against the ALREADY-PUBLISHED `ubx-schema-kubernetes` `v2.0.0`: `kubernetes_ds`'s own real data source type names came out prefixed `kubernetes_ds_` instead of the intended, shared `kubernetes_` prefix -- not caught by Stage D's own earlier verification because that verification checked resource/data-source COUNTS (92/116, both correct) and zero-network behavior, never the actual TYPE NAME SHAPE. Fixed in both functions; the real, committed correction turned out to be a genuinely tiny, one-line-per-file diff (`"wire_name": "kubernetes"` added to each member file) -- `RawSpec` itself was always correct, since wire_name only affects translation at load time, never what gets fetched/stored. New regression test (`TestGenerateOpenAPIMember_WireNameOverride_RealDistinctTypeNames`) guards against this recurring silently.

**A second, real, NEW finding: fixing the bug makes Datadog's own real v1/v2 collision visible for the first time, and it now correctly blocks a single combined pin.** Regenerated Datadog's own not-yet-published snapshot with the fix and ran it through `MergeOpenAPIGroup`: it refuses loudly with `ErrDuplicateWireType: "datadog_application_key_response" (resource), contributed by member "datadog_v2"` -- exactly the real collision this org's own `sdk/providers/.ubx/config` already documents (`[dynamic_provider_groups.datadog_all].exclude`), previously hidden by the OLD, buggy generation accidentally using different wrong prefixes per member (which never collided, for the wrong reason). This is real, verified progress, not a regression -- the mechanism now correctly detects what the old, buggy one silently missed -- but it means **Datadog's own single-pin resolution cannot work yet**: no precedence/exclude mechanism exists for the PINNED-resolution path today (only `ubx sdk gen`'s own separate, codegen-time exclude table handles this, and it has no bearing on pinning).

**Three real PRs open, none merged (never self-merge)**:
- `ubx-provider-dynamic#19` -- the merge mechanism + the wire_name bug fix. `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean whole-repo, gofmt clean. Verified live: a single `UBX_DYNAMIC_PROVIDER_NAME=kubernetes` launch against the real, regenerated 2-member group now returns 92 resources AND 116 data sources together; referencing `kubernetes_ds` directly now fails loud with a clear message.
- `ubx-schema-kubernetes#4` -- corrects the already-published `v2.0.0`'s own wrong type-name prefixes (2-line diff total) and updates the README to show one pin instead of two. Depends on `#19` for the fix to actually take effect once resolved.
- `ubx-schema-datadog#1` -- updated with the SAME wire_name correction (4-line diff, not yet published so no release correction needed) and an honestly-updated README documenting that Datadog's own real collision blocks a single combined pin today, unlike Kubernetes.

**`cli/dynamicprovider_pinned_live_test.go` rewritten** to prove ONE `[providers.kubernetes]` pin returns both resource and data-source schemas together (was two separate pins) -- hermetic bar stays clean (`go test ./...` whole-repo), but the REAL, live-gated proof against the actual corrected release can't run until `ubx-provider-dynamic#19` merges (the binary that would serve it builds from real `origin/main`) AND `ubx-schema-kubernetes#4` merges AND `v2.0.0` is corrected on the real release (delete+recreate, matching the earlier `v0.1.0` precedent, or a new patch version -- a real, small follow-up decision, not made here).

**Real, open design question for the founder, not decided here**: how should Datadog's (and any future provider's) real v1/v2-style collision be resolved for PINNED merging specifically? Options named, not chosen: (a) build a real precedence/exclude mechanism into the pinned-resolution path itself (a new, real config concept -- where would it live? embedded in the snapshot's own manifest at generation time seems most natural, since the group already knows its own real member list there), (b) some other approach. This blocks Datadog's own single-pin goal specifically; it does NOT block Kubernetes (already fixed) or providers whose real groups happen to have zero internal collisions (unconfirmed for Google/Azure/GitHub -- worth checking before assuming they're collision-free too).

**What's next**: founder review/merge of the three open PRs, and a real decision on the precedence question before Datadog's own group can be pinned as one entry. Stage F is paused here, not abandoned -- the general mechanism this arc built is real, tested, and already proven correct for the collision-free case; only the collision-precedence piece remains, and it is worth deciding deliberately rather than guessing.

All three show the exact same real pattern: `Determine version` logs `committed=<v>, live PyPI=<v>, live npm=<none>` then `sdk/go/v<v> already tagged -- backfilling any missing registry at the same committed version, not bumping`; `Publish to npm` shows a REAL `npm notice Publishing to https://registry.npmjs.org/...` (not skipped); `Publish to PyPI` and `Tag the source commit` both show `<registry> already has <v> -- skipping (backfilling a different registry)` (correctly skipped, not re-uploaded/re-tagged). **One real operational lesson, not a bug**: independent PyPI specific-version queries (`pypi.org/pypi/<project>/<version>/json`) 404'd immediately after several of these publishes (azure, google) despite the workflow's own upload log showing a genuine, successful `twine upload` (real progress bar, real "View at: https://pypi.org/project/.../<version>/" confirmation URL). Retried with backoff instead of concluding failure -- resolved within 20-40 seconds every time. PyPI's specific-version JSON endpoint has real, live propagation lag distinct from the main upload succeeding; a single immediate 404 there is not evidence of a failed publish, matches this project's own already-documented finding that PyPI verification needs a real retry window, not a one-shot check.

**AWS's own verify-step bug (named at the end of the prior entry) fixed**: `Verify registries agree`'s own Go proxy query hardcoded `.../sdk/go/@v/...`, never accounting for `go.mod`'s own real `/v2` module suffix (Go's required convention once a module's major version is 2+, which AWS's real `go.mod` already declares post-UBI-98). Fixed by reading the real module path from `go.mod` directly at verify time instead of hardcoding it -- also means this never goes stale again on a future v3+ bump, not just patched for v2 specifically. Verified against the real, already-published `v2.0.0`: the derived path resolves correctly on the real Go proxy. PR `ubx-sdk-aws#14`, open, not merged.

## UBI-185 follow-up: AWS genuinely published (npm/PyPI/Go all agree at 2.0.0), but its first real publish deleted a real committed file -- fixed, restored, PRs open, azure/datadog/github/google/kubernetes not yet re-dispatched, 2026-08-26

**Scope**: all seven prior PRs merged. Dispatch the six provider repos one at a time, verifying each against npm/PyPI/Go proxy directly rather than trusting the workflow's own exit status, per the founder's own explicit instruction. Expected: aws 2.0.0, azure 1.0.0, datadog 1.1.0, github 1.1.0, google 1.1.0, kubernetes 1.0.0.

**AWS dispatched first -- genuinely published, all three registries independently confirmed to agree**: `npm registry.npmjs.org/@ubx%2fsdk-aws/2.0.0` -> `2.0.0`; `pypi.org/pypi/ubx-sdk-aws/2.0.0/json` -> `2.0.0`; Go proxy (queried at the REAL module path, `.../sdk/go/v2/@v/v2.0.0.info` -- go.mod declares `module .../sdk/go/v2`, confirmed before querying rather than assumed) -> `v2.0.0`. All three genuinely agree.

**The workflow's own final "Verify registries agree" step reported failure anyway -- a real, AWS-specific, pre-existing bug in that step's own Go proxy query, not a publish problem**: that step's own `curl` still queries `.../sdk/go/@v/v$version.info` (no `/v2`), which 404s / resolves the wrong module for any v2+ Go module -- confirmed the actual run: npm, PyPI, and the Go tag all showed `success`, `Commit version bump` shows `success` (so `main` genuinely carries the real, published version), and only `Verify registries agree` shows `failure`. Exactly why the founder's own instruction was to verify independently rather than trust the exit status -- confirmed live, not hypothetical. Not fixed this session (cosmetic -- the commit already landed by the time this step runs, so a false failure here can't corrupt anything) -- named as a real follow-up, not silently left for the next person to rediscover.

**A third, more serious bug found immediately after, before dispatching anything else -- real data loss on AWS's own real `main`, caught and reverted the same session**: `git log` on AWS's real `sdk/typescript/package.json` showed the "bump to v2.0.0" commit **deleted the file** (9 lines removed, not modified). Root cause: `build-npm.mjs`'s own `npm install --no-save` step mutates the real, committed `package.json` as an npm side effect regardless of `--no-save`; the script's own `rmSync` afterward discarded it entirely rather than restoring it, and nothing downstream ever put it back before "Commit version bump" `git add`-ed whatever was left on disk -- nothing, after the delete. This bug already existed before this session (untouched by any of the prior fixes), but had never actually been exercised end to end successfully for any of the six repos until AWS's dispatch just now -- confirmed directly: datadog/github/kubernetes's own `main` still has their `package.json` intact, from an earlier, different commit that predates npm ever being wired in (their 2026-08-24 publish never reached this step for real).

**Fixed at the root, verified locally before applying, and would have compounded across all five remaining repos if not caught here first**: `build-npm.mjs` now saves the real file's content before `npm install` runs and writes it back verbatim afterward, instead of discarding it. Verified by actually running the fixed script locally (azure, which still had an intact `package.json` to test against) and diffing before/after: byte-identical. Applied identically to all six repos (byte-identical `md5sum` before and after, matching this project's own "port the fix to the whole family" convention) -- PRs `ubx-sdk-aws#12`, `ubx-sdk-azure#13`, `ubx-sdk-datadog#9`, `ubx-sdk-github#10`, `ubx-sdk-google#16`, `ubx-sdk-kubernetes#10`. Separately restored AWS's own already-deleted file on a second PR (`ubx-sdk-aws#13`) from its last real, committed content (already at the correct 2.0.0, no further bump needed).

**Also checked, before reporting, whether this same pipeline would produce a misleading commit for the three backfill-only repos once the fix lands**: replicated the "Bump version" step's own rewrite logic locally against datadog's real, current files with the version held constant (1.1.0 -> 1.1.0, the real no-op case for datadog/github/kubernetes) -- `package.json`/`deno.json`/`pyproject.toml` all come back byte-identical to their current committed content. Confirms the "Commit version bump" step will correctly detect nothing changed and skip committing for these three once the deletion fix is in place, not produce a hollow "bump" commit with nothing real behind it.

Independently re-verified after the fact, not trusting the green run: `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@ubx%2fsdk/1.0.0` returns `version: 1.0.0` for real, `dist-tags.latest` agrees. This was a real prerequisite, not a formality -- all six provider repos declare a real npm dependency on this package (never vendored).

**Before touching any of the six provider repos, surveyed all of them first -- a real version-decision landmine found and NOT walked into blind**: querying live PyPI/Go-proxy state directly (not trusting the committed version alone) showed AWS/Azure/Google's committed versions genuinely ahead of live (safe, would publish as-is) -- but Datadog/GitHub/Kubernetes's committed versions EXACTLY MATCH live PyPI and the live Go tag already (published 2026-08-24, before npm was ever wired into the workflow -- only npm is missing for these three). Traced the actual bash logic in `publish.yml` by hand: `committed == live` falls through to the ROUTINE PATCH-bump branch, which would have republished all three registries one version ahead of what the founder actually asked for (1.1.1/1.1.1/1.0.1, not 1.1.0/1.1.0/1.0.0). Flagged this to the founder before proceeding (AskUserQuestion) rather than guessing; founder chose "patch the workflow first."

**AWS: a second, repo-specific bug found on the very first real dispatch, before any registry was touched**: `workflow_dispatch` failed at the version-bump step -- `FileNotFoundError: sdk/typescript/deno.json`. AWS is the only one of the six repos missing this file (confirmed: all five others have it); `build-npm.mjs` treats it as the single source of truth for the real npm manifest, so no AWS npm publish could ever have succeeded. Reconstructed directly from the already-committed `sdk/typescript/aws/` tree (2006 `.ts` files, one export entry each, matching every other repo's own key/value convention exactly) -- not regenerated from a live source, zero schema drift introduced. Verified by actually running `build-npm.mjs` locally against the reconstructed file (`UBX_SDK_RUNTIME_VERSION=^1.0.0`, the real, now-published `@ubx/sdk`): built cleanly, 2006/2006 exports, `dist/package.json` correct. PR `ubx-sdk-aws#10`, open, `CLEAN`/`MERGEABLE`, not merged.

**A second, universal bug found on Azure's real dispatch -- would have blocked every one of the six repos, not just Azure**: with AWS's deno.json issue not yet fixed, tried Azure next (has a real deno.json already) -- failed at "Publish to npm" with a real npm registry error: `E422 ... Error verifying sigstore provenance bundle: Failed to validate repository information: package.json: "repository.url" is ""`. `npm publish --access public --provenance` cross-checks the built `dist/package.json`'s own `repository.url` against the real GitHub Actions run's repo -- `build-npm.mjs` never wrote one. Confirmed universal, not Azure-specific, by checking directly: all six repos' `build-npm.mjs` are byte-identical (same `md5sum`) and none had a `repository` field. `ubx-sdk-typescript`'s own already-published `package.json` (hand-committed, not built fresh) already carries one, which is why the runtime publish succeeded and none of the providers' would have. Fixed by deriving `repository.url` from the package name (`@ubx/sdk-<provider>` -> `git+https://github.com/Ubiquex/ubx-sdk-<provider>.git`), verified live by rebuilding Azure's package locally and inspecting the real `dist/package.json` for the field.

**Both the version-decision gap and the provenance bug fixed together, and a THIRD problem found while designing the fix, not after**: fixing the version-decision branch alone (make it choose `committed` instead of bumping) would still have broken on re-run for Datadog/GitHub/Kubernetes -- the "Tag the source commit" step would try to re-create an ALREADY-EXISTING git tag (hard error), and "Publish to PyPI" would try to re-upload an ALREADY-EXISTING PyPI release (PyPI rejects re-uploads of an existing version outright). Made each of the three publish steps (npm/PyPI/Go tag) independently check-before-publish -- skip with a clear message if that exact version is already live on that specific registry, otherwise publish -- so the workflow is safe to re-run against a partially-published version regardless of which registry is the one missing, not just today's specific shape. Traced the patched version-decision logic by hand against Datadog's own real committed/live state (`new_version=1.1.0`, confirmed correct) before trusting it.

**Applied identically to all six repos, verified byte-identical before AND after** (matching this project's own established "port the fix to the whole family" convention): `build-npm.mjs` md5sums identical across all six pre-fix and post-fix; each `publish.yml` diff reviewed for one repo (Datadog) and confirmed structurally identical for the rest via the same generation script; all six YAML files parse clean.

**Verified both failed real dispatches (AWS, Azure) left zero side effects**: both failed before any registry write (AWS at the version-bump step, Azure at the npm publish step) -- every downstream step (`Publish to PyPI`, `Tag the source commit`, `Commit version bump`) shows `skipped`, matching the workflow's own designed fail-safe (commit only after every publish succeeds). Confirmed directly against npm itself, not just the run log: `@ubx/sdk-azure` still 404s on the registry, no orphaned/partial entry from the rejected publish.

The data source artifact work (six providers, this session, prior to this arc) never touched these keys -- confirmed structurally, not just empirically: PR#12's own keys are all nested RESOURCE field paths (nothing depth-0, see below), while the data source work's own keys are exclusively `data_`-prefixed -- disjoint namespaces by construction, not a coincidence that happened to hold this one time.

**Verified the fix was real, not just smaller**: diff line counts now match the exact arithmetic expected from the entries actually touched (GCP: 24,759 renames x 2 lines/rename = 49,518, matching exactly; every other provider's number matches its own rename-count/import-count arithmetic the same way). **Root cause, confirmed for all 272, not assumed to generalize from the one sample**: every one of the 272 has a key in `artifacts/azure/intros.json` that `azure_corrected_wire` collapses to exactly the page's current wire (e.g. `azure_appconfiguration_appconfiguration_configuration_store` -> `azure_appconfiguration_configuration_store`). `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s typeName synthesis stopped doubling these specific wires at some point after UBI-175 Phase C authored the original intros against the then-current (doubled) form; the page itself was regenerated afterward under the corrected wire, but the artifact's own key was never renamed to follow. Confirmed via a reverse search (does any current `intros.json` key collapse to this target wire) across all 272 -- zero unexplained. This is a real, previously-unknown class of drift `coverage_check.py` doesn't yet check for directly (it widens a SCHEMA wire to try its corrected form, but never tries the reverse -- whether an ARTIFACT key collapses to match a schema wire) -- worth folding into the checker itself as a follow-up, not done this session since the immediate ask was finding and fixing the live instances, not hardening the checker against the next one.

**Backfilled from the page, not from the stale key's own text, per the explicit instruction**: extracted each page's real intro text by reversing `gen_provider_docs.py`'s own `intro_and_description` three cases (real split / a genuinely single-sentence intro deliberately duplicated between frontmatter and body by Phase 6's own design / a truncated frontmatter description that isn't a literal prefix of the source) -- a blind concatenation of frontmatter description + body would have doubled the wire's own self-reference in two of the three cases; verified zero double self-references across all 272 before applying, then spot-checked 6 random extractions by hand.

**Verified as a true no-op beyond the intended rekey**: `git diff --stat` on the applied change is exactly 272 insertions / 272 deletions, no reformatting of untouched entries. Re-ran `coverage_check.py --only azure`: missing-intro 295 -> 23, exactly the 272 fixed; total Azure gaps 333 -> 61. The remaining 23 are genuine (11 real fresh-authoring gaps, 12 the already-known, already-unpublished `network/virtualnetwork` family -- explicitly deferred, per the founder's own instruction, to its own pass alongside the AWS `_index` orphans).

**Committed and pushed, PR open, not merged (never self-merge)**: branch `fix/azure-intros-stale-doubled-keys`, `ubiquex-docs#43`, based on current `main`. Verified `MERGEABLE` (`UNSTABLE` is Mintlify's own pending preview-deploy check, the same already-established benign reading from every prior PR in this arc).

**Follow-up 2, the seven GCP batch branches -- report only, nothing merged or discarded**: `gh pr list` initially looked alarming (PRs #17-23 all show `state: MERGED`) until checked against each PR's own real `baseRefName` -- every one of batches 2 through 8 is based on the PREVIOUS batch's own branch, not `main` (batch3 based on batch2, batch4 on batch3, ...), the identical stacked-PR shape already established by the AWS/Azure/GCP data-source-artifacts arc earlier this session. Nobody ever opened a final PR from the batch8 tip to `main` -- confirmed via `gh pr list`, no such PR exists, open or closed.

**Not stale, not superseded -- confirmed forgotten, with dates**: `git merge-base` between `main` and the batch8 tip is exactly `6661aa52` (batch1's own landing commit) -- the whole stack branched off the instant batch1 merged and has had zero commits since (`git log -1` on every branch in the stack: 2026-08-24 23:04-23:10, all seven within one seven-minute window, none touched again in the two days since). `main` has moved 33 commits ahead in that time (the UBI-189 six-provider data-source-artifacts arc, the generator scope-guard fix, this session's own UBI-187 work) while the batch stack gained zero. Content freshness already independently confirmed by this session's own earlier coverage-check run: the ~460 GCP "schema entry, no page" gaps it found are these exact resources, still present in the CURRENT schema dump -- not superseded by any later upstream API change.

**Real merge risk found and scoped, not just asserted safe**: simulated the actual merge (`git merge --no-commit --no-ff` against a scratch clone of current `main`, never pushed) rather than trusting GitHub's own `mergeable: UNKNOWN` field, which reflects a stale/uncomputed state for a comparison GitHub has never actually run. Exactly one file conflicts, `docs.json`, in 72 separate blocks out of 460 total files the merge would touch -- `categories.json`/`intros.json`/`manifest.json`/every resource-reference page auto-merge clean. A blind "resolve conflicts, take the union" pass across all 72 blocks would get this one specific block wrong and inject GCP paths into AWS's nav group -- exactly the kind of `docs.json` corruption the generator scope-guard PR (`#41`, this session) was built to catch on the GENERATOR side, not something to reintroduce by hand on the merge side.

**Not merged, not discarded -- the founder's own call, as asked**: nothing about this stack's content is stale or superseded; it's real, current, validated GCP alpha/beta coverage sitting one deliberate merge away from landing. ## ubiquex-docs: generator refuses to write shared files outside its declared scope, root cause found for two of three incidents, 2026-08-26

**Scope**: the founder named three real, live incidents where running `ubiquex-docs`' own resource-reference page generator against a filtered subset rewrote things outside that subset -- the GCP landing page clobbered to the last family processed; 7 unrelated pages plus an index overwritten during the `google_dlp_job` rename; two rounds of accidental AWS resource-page deletion during data source generation cleanup. Every one was caught by human inspection, never by the tool refusing. Asked to report where the unscoped writes originate (more than one path suspected) and make the generator refuse to write outside its declared scope. `generate_richer_provider` unconditionally overwriting the provider index was already named as one confirmed cause going in; the AWS deletions and the dlp rename were flagged as possibly having different causes.

**Root cause, confirmed and singular for two of the three incidents**: `generate_richer_provider` (`ubiquex-docs/scripts/resource-reference-gen/gen_provider_docs.py`) built `resource-reference/<provider>/index.mdx` and every `resource-reference/<provider>/<service>/index.mdx` directly from its own `schema` argument, unconditionally, on every call. Every real caller (`regen_pages.py` above all -- one call per real `[dynamic_providers.<family>]` entry, confirmed by reading the loop directly) only ever gives it one family's own slice, never the whole provider corpus, even on a run whose own families list happens to cover every family. Rebuilding a SHARED, cross-family file from a single family's own partial view silently discards every other family's card entries -- this is the confirmed mechanism behind both the GCP landing-page clobber and the index-page half of the `google_dlp_job` incident (the 7-sibling collateral in that same incident is `gcp_corrected_local`'s own per-API correction scope, a real but separate, already-accepted granularity choice -- regenerating a whole family's own pages when fixing one resource in it, not a scope VIOLATION under the founder's own new definition, since siblings within the declared family aren't "another family's pages").

**The AWS deletion incident, investigated, NOT conclusively root-caused, reported honestly rather than guessed**: grepped every `.py` file in `ubiquex-docs/scripts/resource-reference-gen/` for `os.remove`/`shutil.rmtree`/`.unlink(`/`os.rmdir` -- exactly one hit, `verify_go_blocks.py`, an unrelated Go-build tempdir cleanup. No script in the repository contains any file-deletion logic touching `.mdx` pages at all. `gen_all_data_source_pages.py` (the "data source generation" tool this incident's own name points at) was read end to end: its only writes are `resource-reference/<provider>/data/<service_dir>/<slug>.mdx` paths derived directly from its own `go_idents` scan, and a `docs.json` patch that only mutates the touched provider's own matched groups in place (`groups = provider_group(doc, provider_key)`, a reference into the loaded doc, not a full rebuild) -- confirmed safe by direct reading, not assumed. `move_legacy.py`/`move_legacy2.py` (real scratch tools from earlier GCP/Azure legacy-split work) use `git mv` only, explicitly document "nothing is deleted," and never touch AWS at all. STATE.md's own accessible history (this same file) documents the dlp-rename incident in detail but never separately narrates an AWS-specific deletion episode with enough detail to trace a mechanism from. Reported as genuinely unresolved rather than fabricating a matching story -- the fix below refuses this whole CLASS of incident regardless of its exact undocumented cause, but the specific prior mechanism was not found.

**Fix**: `generate_richer_provider` no longer writes either aggregate file, full stop -- not behind a flag, removed from the function entirely. Per-resource page writes now pass through a new `_assert_within_scope` guard that raises (real refusal, not a logged warning) if a computed path resolves outside the provider's own `out_root`. A new, separate function, `rebuild_provider_index`, derives both aggregate files from the REAL, CURRENT file tree on disk (globs every service directory, reads each real page's own `title:` frontmatter for its wire type) rather than any one call's own schema -- safe regardless of whether a run covers one family or every family, since it can never discard a family it didn't itself scan. Wired into both real callers that relied on the old unconditional behavior: `regen_pages.py` (called once after its own per-family loop finishes) and `gen_new_provider_pages.py` (called once after its own single generation call).

**Verified, not assumed clean**: new `verify_scope_guard.py` (checked in, `ubiquex-docs/scripts/resource-reference-gen/`) reproduces the real incident shape end to end against a throwaway `docs_root`, never the real repo -- seeds an "already-published" family (2 resources, its own service index, its own provider index), runs a scoped `generate_richer_provider` call for a DIFFERENT, single new family, and confirms via direct byte-for-byte comparison that the first family's own `index.mdx`/service-index/resource pages are untouched afterward (the real bug: before this fix, they weren't). Separately confirms the scope guard raises on a crafted `"../"` path escape and allows a real in-scope path. Confirms `rebuild_provider_index` correctly reconstructs the provider index reflecting BOTH families (3 total resources, not just the one this run touched) without dropping the untouched family's own resource pages. All 11 checks pass. Every touched/new file syntax-checks and imports cleanly alongside the other real callers (`gen_complete_pages.py`, `gen_golden_page.py`) that don't call `generate_richer_provider` at all, confirming no accidental breakage there.

**Committed and pushed, PR open, not merged (never self-merge)**: branch `fix/generator-scope-guard`, `ubiquex-docs#41`, based on current `main`. Verified `CLEAN`/`MERGEABLE`. Zero real `resource-reference/`, `docs.json`, or `artifacts/` content touched -- scripts and the new verification tool only.

**What's next**: the founder's own call on merging `#41`. If the specific AWS-deletion mechanism is ever identified (a git commit reference, a more specific recollection of which tool was run), it's worth a follow-up regardless of this fix already covering the general class -- knowing the exact prior cause is still real, useful information this session couldn't recover on its own.

## UBI-178 piece 4 follow-up: fakeprovider data source fixture built, immediately caught a real, separate missing-runtime-type bug, 2026-08-26

**Scope**: the founder flagged a real gap in this session's own earlier UBI-190/consumer-test work -- no fakeprovider mode ever served a real `DataSourceSchemas` entry, so `provider.Schemas.DataSources` was always empty through the real `ubx sdk gen` CLI path. Coverage until now was `ir` derivation plus each language's own generated-output checks, hermetic but stopping short of the actual command path -- exactly why the original ResourceBinding/DataSourceBinding template swap (UBI-178 piece 4) shipped through `go build`/`deno check`/`ast.parse` unnoticed: none of those checks ever called the generated code, and nothing ever generated a real data source to check.

**Fixture built**: `fake_widget` now names both a resource and a data source in fakeprovider's `ok-v6`/`ok-v5` modes (`provider/internal/fakeprovider/main.go`), deliberately reusing the identical name -- mirroring `hashicorp/aws`'s own `aws_instance` being both, per `ir.ResourceType.IsDataSource`'s own doc comment -- so the fixture exercises the real same-WireType collision the `data` namespace segment exists to prevent, not just a lone data source in isolation. Shape deliberately asymmetric from the resource (`name` Required, `id`/`tags` Computed, vs the resource's `tags` Optional) so field-split assertions can't pass by copy-paste accident.

**Immediately caught a real, separate bug building it, not a contrived one**: with the fixture wired in, `ubx sdk gen --lang go` against it produced code referencing `ubx.DataSourceBinding` -- but the pinned `sdk/go/runtime` submodule commit (`ef3fded`) had NO such type at all, so a real `go build` failed outright (`undefined: ubx.DataSourceBinding`). TypeScript hit the identical gap (`deno check`: `has no exported member named 'DataSourceBinding'`). Root cause, checked directly rather than assumed: all three real, separate runtime repos (`ubx-sdk-go`, `ubx-sdk-typescript`, `ubx-sdk-python`) already had `DataSourceBinding`/`Data()` merged into their own real `main` branches -- each confirmed via the GitHub API directly (`gh api repos/Ubiquex/ubx-sdk-<lang>/commits/main`), not inferred from a local copy, matching CLAUDE.md's own rule 8 discipline -- this monorepo's own `sdk/go`/`sdk/ts`/`sdk/py` submodule pointers were simply never bumped to consume any of them (`ef3fded`->`73f7fa4` go, `29f4825`->`00ce8e0` ts, `3d3bcf1`->`c509641` py, all three real `main` tips). Python's own pinned commit already had the fix (Python's own PR had merged earlier); Go and TS did not.

**This is a real, separate finding from the fixture-building work itself**: `consumer_test.go`'s own doc comment claims its hand-written stand-in runtime's public surface was "confirmed live against the real, separate ubx-sdk-go repo before writing this" -- true of the real repo's `main` as of whenever that was written, but the monorepo's own checked-out copy had drifted behind it since, and nothing in this repo's own test suite would have caught that drift without a test that actually compiles against the real, separate submodule content rather than a hermetic fixture standing in for it.

**New end-to-end test**: `TestSDKGen_GeneratesDataSourceBindingsFromRealSchema_ViaMirror` (`cli/sdk_test.go`) runs all three languages through the real CLI against the fixture, asserts each generated data-source file carries the correct binding type and the resource file carries the correct other one, then compiles/typechecks/imports the generated trees against the real, separate runtime repos (git submodules, not a stand-in) -- `assertGoRepoCompiles`/`assertTSRepoChecks`/`assertPyRepoImports`, the same real-compile helpers the existing per-language resource tests already use. **Confirmed load-bearing, not just present**: temporarily reintroduced the exact historical binding swap in all three templates (`go.go`/`ts.go`/`py.go`), ran the new test, watched it fail immediately (on the string check, before even reaching the compile step), reverted, confirmed clean again.

**What it catches that the current tests do not, the founder's own explicit ask**: (1) that `provider.Schemas.DataSources` actually flows through `writeGeneratedSDK`'s real `IsDataSource=true` branch and `ir.FromSchema` against a REAL provider-served schema, not a hand-built `ir.ResourceType{IsDataSource: true}` literal -- the hermetic `ir`/template tests never construct one from an actual wire fetch; (2) that the generated code for a data source actually COMPILES/TYPECHECKS against the REAL, separate `ubx-sdk-go`/`ubx-sdk-typescript` runtime repos, not `consumer_test.go`'s own hand-maintained stand-in -- which is exactly what caught the stale-submodule gap above, something no existing test could have found since every existing Go/TS check either used the hermetic fixture or never generated a data source at all; (3) that a resource and a data source sharing the identical WireType land at genuinely different generated paths under one real CLI run, not just that `ir.ServiceAndLocalNameForType` returns different strings in a unit test.

**Fallout, mechanical, not a finding**: three pre-existing tests' own `"generated 1 resource type(s)"` stdout assertions bumped to `"generated 2 resource type(s)"` -- the correct, expected result of `fake_widget` now also being a real data source, not a regression.

**Verified**: `go build ./...` clean, full `go test ./...` clean (every package, not just `cli`). Submodule bumps verified against the real, separate repos' GitHub API `main` tips directly, not inferred.

**Committed and pushed, PR open, not merged (never self-merge)**: branch `fix/ubi-178-fakeprovider-datasource-fixture`, `ubiquex#29`, based on current `main`, two commits (submodule bump; fixture+test). Verified `CLEAN`/`MERGEABLE`.

**Note, unrelated to this session's work**: `sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json` still carries the same pre-existing uncommitted local modification flagged in the prior two sessions' own entries -- left untouched again, not investigated, not this session's.

## UBI-190: Datadog dump-ir nondeterminism diagnosed and fixed -- genuinely ordering-dependent, not GCP-shaped, 2026-08-26

**Scope**: the founder's own instruction split this into two real problems and named the second as the real one: (1) two Datadog resources resolving to the same generated name, (2) WHICH one loses varying between identical runs, a real map-iteration-order violation of CLAUDE.md's own determinism rule and a real threat to UBI-182's snapshot hashing. Asked explicitly to check whether this was the same shape as the earlier GCP nondeterminism (Google's own backend returning different content between fetches, not code) or genuinely ordering-dependent, by running against a cached spec so the input cannot vary -- and to report the cause before fixing.

**Problem 1, real but already mitigated in config, not the actual bug**: `sdk/providers/.ubx/config`'s own `[dynamic_provider_groups.datadog_all.exclude]` table already documents and excludes Datadog's two real, live v1/v2 resource-name collisions (`datadog_application_key_response`, `datadog_user_response` -- v1's own richer version wins both, per that table's own comment). Confirmed live: 4 consecutive runs against the real, current config succeeded cleanly, 704 resource types each time, no collision at all -- the exclude table is currently complete against Datadog's live spec.

**Problem 2, the real one, root-caused to `cli/sdk.go`'s own `mergeDynamicProviderGroupMembers`**: both its Resources and DataSources merge loops iterated `m.schemas.Resources`/`m.schemas.DataSources` (plain `map[string]*provider.Schema`) directly via `range` and returned on the FIRST collision found. Go deliberately randomizes map iteration order per range call -- with two or more real, simultaneous collisions present in one merge, which one this loop hits first (and therefore which one the error names) depends purely on that randomized order, not on the data.

**Verified as genuinely ordering-dependent, not GCP-shaped, before writing a single line of fix**, exactly as asked: built a clean `ubx-provider-dynamic` binary from a git-worktree copy of its own current HEAD (the pre-existing, unrelated uncommitted WIP already sitting in that checkout -- `typename/dlp-triple-repeat-fix` branch, `internal/{discoverydoc,resourcemap,smithy}/datasource*.go` -- left completely untouched, confirmed intact after), pinned the fetched Datadog spec bytes via `UBX_PROVIDER_DYNAMIC_FETCH_CACHE` (the exact mechanism the earlier GCP investigation built for this exact purpose), forced the two normally-excluded collisions back into play in a scratch copy of the config (real config, real live spec, only the `exclude` list edited), and ran the identical command three times against that byte-identical, cache-pinned input with the identical binary: reported `datadog_application_key_response` twice, `datadog_user_response` once. Same input, same binary, different answer -- conclusively rules out backend drift (Google's shape) and confirms the code itself is the cause.

**Fix**: sort each member's typeName keys before iterating, in both loops -- the same discipline `resourcemap.go`'s own `Discover` already applies to its own `byBase` map (`sort.Strings(bases)` before iterating) for the identical reason, just missing from this later, group-level merge step. Re-ran the same forced-collision scratch test 5 times post-fix: reported the identical, alphabetically-first `datadog_application_key_response` every time. Re-ran the real, current config (excludes intact) post-fix: still 704 resource types, unchanged. New regression test, `TestMergeDynamicProviderGroupMembers_MultipleCollisions_ReportsSameOneEveryRun`, rebuilds the exact live two-collision shape 50 times and asserts an identical error every run -- confirmed it fails on the pre-fix code (5/5 runs, verified via `git stash`) and passes on the fix. Full `go test ./cli/...` clean.

**Scope beyond Datadog, named not fixed**: the same unsorted-iterate-then-fail-fast pattern applies to every `dynamic_provider_group` (`google_all`, `azure_all`, ...), not just Datadog's -- a structural risk in the merge code itself, not a Datadog-specific bug. Datadog is simply the only group currently known to carry two or more real, live collisions at once; the fix protects every group equally since it's in the shared merge function, not a Datadog-specific patch.

**Committed and pushed, PR open, not merged (never self-merge)**: branch `fix/ubi-190-datadog-group-merge-determinism`, `ubiquex#28`, based on current `main`. Verified `CLEAN`/`MERGEABLE`. Scoped to exactly the two intended files (`cli/sdk.go`, `cli/dynamicprovidergroup_test.go`) -- the separate, pre-existing, unrelated uncommitted `sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json` modification (flagged in an earlier entry, still unexplained, still not this session's) was left out of the commit and remains untouched in the working tree.

**A real miss, not a deliberate exclusion, caught and corrected this session**: the prior session's own AWS entry (below) reported the whole UBI-189 multi-provider data-source-artifact effort complete after five providers (Kubernetes 75, GitHub 249, Datadog 445, Azure 1606, AWS 4526 = 6901). The founder flagged that all six providers have data sources and GCP (411) was never actioned. Verified by arithmetic against this same file's own original scope statement ("write real intros/descriptions for the 7,312 real data source pages"): 7312 - 6901 = 411, exactly GCP's own data source count -- confirming GCP was in scope from the start and was genuinely missed, not skipped for a real reason. The AWS entry below is left as originally written, with a correction note added rather than rewritten, so the miss stays visible in the record rather than quietly disappearing.

**Scope**: same approach applied to GCP's 411 data sources -- sibling-derived intros first, then fresh intros, then depth-0 field descriptions, with the founder's own explicit reminder to verify GCP's own basename convention before trusting any matcher, since three providers already had a heuristic silently fail on their own naming (Datadog's JSON:API envelope overlap, Azure's service_dir double-strip, AWS's CFN-vs-Smithy divergence).

**GCP's own basename convention verified live, a real and different failure mode found before it shipped**: a first-pass token-overlap matcher (same technique as AWS's) found 10 exact + 81 high-overlap matches, but manual review surfaced a real, GCP-specific false-positive class the algorithm alone didn't catch: 122 of 411 (30%) GCP data source local slugs carry a leading API-version token (`alpha_`/`beta_`/`v1_`/...), and letting that token count toward the Jaccard score let unrelated resources match purely on sharing a version, worst example `google_compute_beta_machine_type` scoring high-overlap against `beta-machine-image` (shared only "beta"+"machine", "type" vs "image" are unrelated GCP concepts -- a SKU/type catalog vs a saved VM image). Fixed by extracting the version token separately, requiring it match exactly on both sides when present, and scoring the remaining tokens only. Re-run: 93 raw candidates (12 exact + 81 high-overlap).

**All 93 candidates individually reviewed against real GCP product knowledge, not trusted from the score alone**: 35 rejected. Two real failure categories found, both now worth watching for on any future GCP work: (1) SKU/type-catalog endpoints (`disk_type`, `machine_type`, `network_profile`, `storage_pool_type`, `processor_type`, `notification_channel_descriptor`) wrongly matched to the base resource instance -- a catalog of available types/capabilities is a categorically different concept from an actual instance of that resource, even though they share a name stem; (2) two cross-directory matches (`google_aiplatform_model`/`v1beta1_model` -> `ml/model`, `google_cloudcontrolspartner_workload`/`v1beta_workload` -> `assuredworkloads/workload`) where the matched sibling page lived in a DIFFERENT service directory and its own real intro text described a different, unrelated API -- `google_ml_model`'s own intro explicitly says "on the legacy AI Platform (ML Engine) service," which would have misdescribed the modern Vertex AI aiplatform.googleapis.com API had it been mechanically reused. Also rejected: `backup` vs `backup-plan`/`rollout` vs `rollout-plan` pairs (an instance vs its own template/schedule, a different resource), and a handful of single-generic-token coincidences (`config`, `store`, `service`, `job`, `scope`) that only looked related because GCP's own vocabulary reuses these words across unrelated services. Final: 58 sibling-derived, 353 fresh-authored orphans (batched by real GCP product family: Compute alpha/beta variants, Vertex AI, Firebase App Check, Document AI, Discovery Engine, and roughly 60 more services).

**A real key-format bug caught before the PR was opened, not after**: the first intro-insertion pass stripped the `google_` provider prefix before building the artifact key (matching the internal convention used to author the sibling/fresh dictionaries), producing keys like `data_apigee_app` instead of the generator's own real expected format, `data_google_apigee_app` (confirmed directly from `gen_all_data_source_pages.py`'s own `data_key = f"data_{wire}"` where `wire` is the FULL WireType including the provider prefix). This silently left every one of the 411 pages showing the old boilerplate intro despite the artifact file itself looking correct and complete -- caught only by spot-diffing a regenerated page before trusting the pass, not by the artifact-file line count alone. Fixed by reverting the bad insertion and rebuilding with the correct `data_google_<rest>` key, confirmed via a full re-diff that zero pages still carry the boilerplate text afterward.

**Depth-0 field descriptions, 826 missing filled, 100% of the real gap, out of 4334 total** -- by far the smallest gap of any provider in this phase (156 distinct missing names, vs low hundreds to nearly six thousand for the other five), confirming the founder's own observation that GCP already carried 81% top-level vendor coverage from earlier UBI-175/186 work before this pass started. Covered by a single explicit dictionary pass, no suffix-fallback tier needed at this scale.

**Verified**: `mint validate` clean; all 411 on-disk `resource-reference/gcp/data/**/*.mdx` pages reachable from nav both directions, zero unreachable, zero orphaned nav entries; `docs.json` zero-line diff; zero pages still carry the old boilerplate intro text (checked directly after the key-format fix, not assumed); `intros.json`/`descriptions.json` diffs verified as pure insertions with zero collisions and zero corruption of the 1086/57380 pre-existing entries.

**Committed and pushed, PR open, not merged (never self-merge)**: branch `docs/gcp-data-source-artifacts`, `ubiquex-docs#40`, branched fresh off current `origin/main` (independent of the still-unmerged AWS branch/PR `#39`, since GCP touches only `artifacts/gcp/`/`resource-reference/gcp/`, no file overlap). Manifest dated entry (`ubi189_data_source_artifacts_2026_08_26`) added to both `descriptions` and `intros` sections documenting the missed-scope correction, the version-token matcher fix, and the 35 rejected candidates.

**This actually completes the entire UBI-189 follow-up multi-provider effort**: Kubernetes (75) -> GitHub (249) -> Datadog (445) -> Azure (1606) -> AWS (4526) -> GCP (411) = 7312, matching this file's own original scope statement exactly. **Depth scoped by what a reader actually sees, not assumed**: started `mint dev`, rendered a real page, screenshotted it. Every `<Expandable>` renders collapsed by default at every level -- confirmed live, not from documentation. A reader sees the top-level field name/type/description with zero clicks and nothing else; even depth 1 (the first level of nesting) already requires one. Computed real field/gap counts at depth 0 through 4 (36,180/25,375 gap at depth 0, up to 165,707/143,355 gap at depth 4) and picked depth 0 as the only tier matching "what's actually read" -- smaller than the original GCP+Azure resource gap-fill (97,545), not the larger number depth 4 would have been. Flagged, not silently absorbed: 18 of Azure's 1,606 data sources (the self-referential `network/virtualnetwork` family) account for 91% of Azure's raw uncapped field count from 1% of its resources -- named explicitly so a future uncapped pass doesn't rediscover the explosion; the depth cap already neutralizes it structurally (4.9% share at depth<=4).

Verified zero behavior change for the fallback path before writing any content.

**Doubled intro-prose self-references, the real count**: founder's own spot-check said 272 Azure pages; asked for the real count since a spot-check may undercount. It did, but not for the reason expected -- real total is 276 published pages (272 Azure, 4 GCP), the gap being one Azure family (`azure_azure_kusto_kusto`, 10 resources -- `kusto-cluster.mdx` and 9 siblings) whose own doubled form needs collapsing TWICE (`azure_azure_kusto_kusto_cluster` -> `azure_kusto_kusto_cluster` -> `azure_kusto_cluster`) -- a naive single-pass detector (which is what produces a "272"-shaped undercount) stops after the first pass and still reports a match failure. **Real, load-bearing safety check, not assumed from the collapse algorithm alone**: a generic "leftmost-longest-adjacent-token-repeat collapse" sweep alone is NOT safe to trust blindly -- it flagged 42 AWS and 5 Kubernetes false positives (`aws_access_analyzer_analyzer`, `kubernetes_resource_resource_claim`, `kubernetes_storage_storage_class`) that are real, legitimate, currently-published wire types where the service name and the resource's own local name genuinely share a trailing token, not doubling bugs -- confirmed live by checking each candidate's own real published page (title consistently matches the "doubled-looking" text, not a stale mismatch). The correct, safe test cross-checks every candidate against the corpus's own real, currently-published page titles (10,426 of them, collected once): a reference is only a real bug if collapsing it lands on a title that's REALLY published somewhere and the uncollapsed form is NOT itself a real published title anywhere. AWS/Kubernetes/GitHub/Datadog: zero real bugs, confirmed rather than assumed clean (neither has a correction pass at all, so nothing HAD to be wrong, but nothing was skipped either).

**Fix applied surgically, not via a full JSON re-dump**: a first attempt at the `intros.json` fix used `json.dump(..., indent=1)`, which silently reformatted the WHOLE file (original uses `indent=2`) and produced a 2166-line diff for what was actually 282 real single-entry changes -- caught before committing by checking the diff size against the expected fix count, reverted, redone as a direct string-level patch of only the affected JSON value spans (285 entries total: 282 Azure + 3 GCP, including a few dead duplicate-keyed entries with no live page and a couple already-correct-in-the-artifact-but-never-regenerated pages), landing as exactly 285 changed lines. The 276 affected pages were patched directly (per the generator README's own "an artifact fix alone does not reach already-published pages" rule), 497 total occurrences replaced across frontmatter description + body.

**Verified**: zero doubled self-references remain in any of the six providers' `intros.json` or any published page (re-swept after the fix, not assumed from the fix logic alone). `mint validate`: success, zero warnings. Diff scope confirmed minimal: exactly 276 pages + 2 artifact files, no unrelated churn.

## UBI-186 follow-up: GCP generation nondeterminism (real, external, not a map-ordering bug) + consumer-program verification gap, 2026-08-25

**Context**: founder asked to fix a real finding from UBI-186's own data-source generation work -- three back-to-back full `google_all` regenerations reported 2331/2330/2331 resource types, not the same number every time. Founder's own instinct was CLAUDE.md's standing "no map-iteration ordering" rule. That rule was already being followed: `discoverydoc.go`/`datasource.go`'s own candidate-collision resolution was read line by line and was already fully sorted at every decision point (`sortedKeys`, `sort.Strings`, `firstPrefixedMethod`'s own lexicographic tiebreak) before this session touched anything.

**Real root cause, found not assumed**: a direct two-round fetch of all 262 configured GCP discovery doc URLs found 8 with genuine semantic drift between rounds a few minutes apart -- a live `revision` field moving forward, new schema properties, a newly added method (`compute/v1`'s own `reservationSlots.getHealth`, live-confirmed absent in round 1, present in round 2). This is Google's own live, continuously-deployed backend serving whichever revision happens to be current on the instance that answers a given request -- not this codebase's own iteration order, and not fixable by sorting harder, since the INPUT itself changes between fetches.

**Fix**: `internal/fetchcache` (new package, `ubx-provider-dynamic`) -- an opt-in, on-disk cache in front of `discoverydoc.Load`'s own HTTP fetch, keyed by URL, activated only by `UBX_PROVIDER_DYNAMIC_FETCH_CACHE` naming a directory. Disabled by default (routine single-pass generation is unchanged, still sees the freshest live schema). Verified: three full `google_all --lang go` passes against one warmed cache produced byte-identical output (`diff -rq` clean, 2636 files each); `ts`/`py` passes against the same warm cache now report the identical 2331 count go does.

**Second finding, real and separate**: founder also asked for a "real consumer program" to be added to the verification set, since `go build`/`deno check`/`ast.parse` on a generated repo alone never call `resource()`/`data()` -- exactly how the ResourceBinding/DataSourceBinding mix-up (UBI-178 piece 4 follow-up) shipped silently through all three checks. Added hermetic, per-language consumer tests (`sdk/codegen/templates/{go,ts,py}/consumer_test.go`) against fixtures matching each real, separate runtime's actual contract. **Only Go's is a real, load-bearing check** -- proven by temporarily reintroducing the original binding-swap bug and confirming the new test fails, then restoring the fix. TypeScript and Python are NOT protected by this class of check at all: `deno check` does not reject a `ResourceBinding` passed where a `DataSourceBinding` is expected (both interfaces are structurally identical except for ignored optional phantom fields -- confirmed live, not assumed from the runtime's own doc comment claiming otherwise), and Python's `data()` performs no `isinstance` check at all (confirmed against the real runtime source). Both gaps are now recorded as passing, explicitly-named tests rather than silently assumed -- the real, load-bearing defense for TS/Python remains the generated-source string assertion already in `ts_test.go`/`py_test.go` (`mustContain "DataSourceBinding"`), not the language's own type system.

**A real process finding, not a code bug**: the founder merged the original PRs (`ubx-provider-dynamic#13`, `ubiquex#24`/`#25`, `ubiquex-docs#28`) in the ~1-minute window while this follow-up work was already in progress, before either fix above could land -- so both fixes exist as fresh PRs against current main, not as additions to the now-closed originals: `ubx-provider-dynamic#14` (fetchcache), `ubiquex#26` (consumer tests). Neither merged by this session (never self-merge).

**Docs**: `ubiquex-docs#28`'s own description updated with the real remaining scope, counted directly from `docs.json` rather than estimated -- 635 total service groups across all six providers, 634 remaining after Amplify (AWS 262, GCP 149, Azure 114, Datadog 58, GitHub 29, Kubernetes 22). Not attempted this session -- named as the real, large, separately-scopable next piece, not silently narrowed.

## SDK bindings republish (no Linear ID given for this work): Datadog/GitHub created, AWS/Kubernetes/GCP regenerated, 2026-08-23

**Context**: the six real, separately-published `ubx-sdk-<provider>` repos (combined UBI-138 shape) were stale against the current dynamic-provider corpus -- four still targeted their original `hashicorp/*` Terraform sources or a bare Compute-only Discovery Doc slice, two (Datadog/GitHub) had never been published at all. Founder reviewed a full per-provider report and gave four explicit decisions: create Datadog/GitHub with content-hash versioning; regenerate AWS/GCP/Kubernetes as a `1.0.0` source-change major bump; publish Azure's real `azure_*` corpus replacing `azurerm_*`; archive the 12 dangling per-language legacy repos. Never self-merge; workflow_dispatch publish reserved for the founder.

**Decision 1, done**: `ubx-sdk-datadog` (26 types) and `ubx-sdk-github` (68 types) created under the `Ubiquex` org, seed commit pushed directly (brand-new empty repos, no PR). `VERSION` uses a content-hash scheme (`spec-sha256`/`fetched`/`source`) since neither upstream publishes a discrete release -- both `schema_url`s point at a live branch. `hash-watch.yml` replaces the Terraform-registry-poll `version-watch.yml` pattern for both.

**Real bug found and fixed across all 6 combined repos**: `publish.yml`'s version-decision step only checked "committed ahead of live registry" -- with NO live entry at all (a repo's true first publish), it fell through to the routine PATCH-bump branch and would have published `1.0.1` instead of the committed `1.0.0`. Fixed (treat "no live entry" as its own branch, publish committed as-is) and ported to `ubx-sdk-aws`/`-google`/`-kubernetes`/`-azure` too, each its own PR, confirmed via side-by-side simulation that no behavior changes for a repo with an existing live entry.

Content-hash `VERSION` (CFN registry has no discrete release either).

Built `[dynamic_provider_groups.<name>]` (`cli/sdk.go`: `generateDynamicProviderGroup`/`mergeDynamicProviderGroupMembers`, fail-loud on any real cross-member resource-type collision) -- live-verified against the real 162-member GCP config, caught two real bugs on the first run (group named identically to its own `google` member caused `--only google` to match both and write to the same path; `source` also drives the output directory name via `sanitizeSourceForFilename`, a decorated source string mangled the path) -- both fixed, re-verified, `go build`/`go vet`/full `go test ./cli/...` clean, committed and pushed (`ubiquex@c55908c`, `ubiquex@8062883`). `ubx-sdk-google` then regenerated from all 162 members (880 types, was `hashicorp/google`'s 1333, itself mostly Compute-only) -- real overlap 81/880 (9.2%) against the full corpus, only matches the previously-quoted 81/95 figure when narrowed to just the Compute subset. `VERSION` uses a `merged-schema-sha256` (one hash over the combined, deterministic post-enrichment IR covering all 162 members) since there's no single "GCP version" the way `hashicorp/google@X.Y.Z` was one string. `version-watch.yml` removed (a real 162-member content-hash watch is separate follow-up work, not built this session) rather than left silently watching a source this repo no longer generates from.
