## UBI-180: the uppercase local name -- normalized at the source, swept all 468 providers, 2026-08-23

**Real bug**: `ubx sdk gen` hard-rejected `google_siteverification`'s own real resource -- its raw typeName carried a literal capital, `google_siteverification_siteVerification_web_resource`, because `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own `discoverydoc.go` inserted the live Discovery Document's own `doc.Name` field (Google's real, live-owned string for this one API is `siteVerification`, mixed case) directly into the typeName, unlike the resource-tree key two lines above it -- which already gets the identical real `ToSnakeCase` treatment, for the identical real reason, per that exact fix's own doc comment. `doc.Name` was simply never given the same treatment, since no other real provider's own live `doc.Name` had ever been mixed case until now.

**Decision, made real, not silent**: normalized `doc.Name` at the source (the one place a Discovery Document's own name enters a typeName), not accept-and-escape per language. camelCase-to-snake_case is already the real, deterministic, single-source transformation this whole codebase applies everywhere else for exactly this kind of input (the sibling resource-tree-key fix, `resourcemap.go`'s own `toSnakeCase`, `cloudformation.go`'s own `Resolve`) -- it is not the kind of ambiguous guess the project's own standing "never a best-effort coercion, refuse loudly instead" doctrine (`docs/sdk.md` row 5) exists to refuse. A per-language escape would have tripled the maintenance surface across `sdk/codegen/templates/{go,py,ts}` and risked the three languages silently disagreeing on the resulting identifier -- rejected for that reason, not by default.

**Swept before fixing, per the founder's own instruction, not assumed clean**: a real `--dump-ir` run across all 468 real, top-level configured dynamic providers (not the inflated 474 the raw config grep first suggested -- that count included `[dynamic_providers.<name>.auth]` TOML sub-tables, a real measurement artifact caught and corrected before reporting). `google_siteverification` was the ONLY resource anywhere with an uppercase-carrying WireType or localName -- confirmed by scanning every real, live-dumped `schema.json`, not by reasoning about the code alone. `resourcemap.go` (OpenAPI/Kubernetes/GitHub/Datadog/Azure) and `cloudformation.go`'s own `Resolve` (AWS) were separately read and confirmed to already run every input through their own real `toSnakeCase`/`ToSnakeCase` before it ever reaches a typeName -- this was the one, real, isolated gap.

**Verified live**: go/py/ts codegen all succeed now (previously a hard crash, exit code 2, "1 of 468 dynamic provider(s) failed"). New regression test `TestDiscover_CamelCaseDocName_SnakeCased`. Full `go test ./...` clean. Real typeName: `google_siteverification_site_verification_web_resource` (the word-boundary underscore `ToSnakeCase` inserts means this does NOT collapse under the docs pipeline's own `gcp_corrected_key` doubling-collapse pattern, which needs an exact, case-sensitive prefix match -- a real, separate, minor naming quirk, not a bug, left as-is and noted, not silently absorbed). Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API: `ubx-provider-dynamic@7a28e98`. Never self-merged.

**Docs site**: two stale, pre-existing artifact entries found and cleaned up (`google_siteVerification_web_resource` -- mixed case -- and `google_siteverification_web_resource` -- no underscore -- neither matching the real, now-confirmed key): real, correctly-extracted vendor content moved to the real key rather than re-researched from scratch. Category derived via the same live Discovery-Doc-title method as every other GCP entry. Page generated and verified (`verify_regen_corpus.py` clean, `ast.parse` passes, a real `go build` against the local SDK output succeeds), added to the existing "Site Verification" nav subgroup alongside its own real, separate, pre-existing HashiCorp-era sibling (a different typeName, same real product -- matching this project's established old+new coexistence pattern, not a duplicate). 0 orphans/dangling refs/duplicates, `mint validate` passes. Committed and pushed, verified live: `ubiquex-docs@bbf630a7`.

**Recorded as a standing process note, not just in this log**: the prior turn's "an artifact-level fix does not reach already-published pages" finding is now written directly into `scripts/resource-reference-gen/README.md` itself, not just this file -- a per-session log entry ages out of what a future session actually reads before touching this pipeline; the README is where that session looks first.

## UBI-176 follow-up: real version-priority tie-break (not path-sort) + 187 broken GCP vendor links fixed, 2026-08-23

**Part 1 -- the path-sort tie-break was real but incomplete, not just alpha/beta**: the prior UBI-176 fix recovered 21 dropped resources but still let a naive ReadPath lexicographic sort decide which sibling keeps the plain typeName -- `autoscaling/v2` HorizontalPodAutoscaler (the real, current, preferred API: a multi-metric array replacing v1's single CPU-utilization target) lost to `v1` purely because `"v1" < "v2"` as strings; same for `coordination/v1beta1` LeaseCandidate (lost to the older `v1alpha2`) and `scheduling/v1beta1` PodGroup+Workload (lost to the older `v1alpha3`).

**Checked for a real preferred-version signal, per the founder's own instruction, rather than guessing**: `swagger.json` itself carries none. The same `kubernetes/kubernetes` repo, same release tag, DOES publish one elsewhere -- `api/discovery/apis__<group>.json`'s own real `preferredVersion` field, confirmed live for every affected group (autoscaling -> v2, coordination.k8s.io -> v1, scheduling.k8s.io -> v1). Rather than adding a second live fetch to `resourcemap.go`'s own architecture (Discover takes an already-parsed document, zero I/O of its own today), implemented the identical, real, standard Kubernetes version-priority algorithm (`CompareKubeAwareVersionStrings`: GA beats any prerelease, beta beats alpha, higher number wins within a tier) as a pure comparator -- verified its output matches the real, live discovery signal exactly for all 4 currently-real cases. `Discover` is now two phases: candidates resolved first (unchanged), then grouped by base typeName with the real winner picked by version priority, falling back to the exact pre-existing ReadPath-order tie-break when no group member carries a version token at all (the untouched GitHub/Datadog same-schema-different-path case). New tests, full `go test ./...` clean. Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API: `ubx-provider-dynamic@6e91165`. Never self-merged.

This changed which typeName means what for 4 resources -- `kubernetes_autoscaling_horizontal_pod_autoscaler`/`kubernetes_coordination_lease_candidate`/`kubernetes_scheduling_pod_group`/`kubernetes_scheduling_workload` now correctly mean the current version; the older, still-served sibling moved to a version-qualified name. Rekeyed the already-researched field descriptions for all 4 pairs (real per-version content unchanged, just moved to the right key) and rewrote all 8 intros to be explicit on both sides about which one is current. Closed a further 30-field gap surfaced by the rekey (`scheduling/v1alpha3`'s own live shape has drifted since the original 71-resource corpus was built). Pages regenerated (92/92, determinism verified for the 84 untouched resources), nav and categories.json kept in sync. Verified: 0/1,743 missing across the 8 affected typeNames, 0 orphans/dangling refs/duplicates, `mint validate` passes. Committed and pushed, verified live: `ubiquex-docs@af11ed89`.

**Part 2 -- 187 broken GCP vendor-description links, live count not the quoted estimate**: `docs-vendor` description text carries real markdown links written relative to `cloud.google.com` -- correct on Google's own site, broken root-relative paths on this one. 187 occurrences across 127 fields (83 distinct URL targets), all `source=docs-vendor`, 0 from any other source. Fixed by rewriting to absolute vendor URLs (prepending `https://cloud.google.com`), never stripped, per the founder's own explicit instruction.

Two real, separate data-quality issues found and fixed along the way, both live-verified before applying: a stray trailing quote character baked into the original extracted vendor text (`google_apigee_apidoc.image_url`) and a real, unfilled Google API doc template variable (`google_deploymentmanager_deployment.operation`'s own `{$api_version}`, 3 occurrences) -- substituted with `v1`, Compute Engine's real, current stable API version. 12 of the 83 URLs (`google_ml_job`/`model`/`version`, the legacy AI Platform/ML Engine API) point at real Google documentation that has since been fully retired -- confirmed live, every real `/ai-platform/` candidate replacement redirects to the same generic product hub, not specific content -- left pointing at their real, literal, absolute vendor path rather than fabricating a misleading generic redirect.

**A real architecture gap found and closed, not assumed away**: `regen_pages.py`'s own injection pipeline reads `docs-vendor` text straight from the raw dump-ir schema at generation time, not from `descriptions.json` -- fixing the artifact alone would not have propagated to the 31 already-published pages carrying this same broken text verbatim (193 occurrences, confirmed live by grepping the actual published corpus, not assumed identical to the artifact's own count). Patched both: the artifact (the durable record) and the 31 live `.mdx` pages directly, with the identical fix rules. A further, real bug caught mid-fix: MDX escapes literal curly braces as HTML entities in body text (`{` -> `&#123;`), so the `{$api_version}` fix's plain string replace silently missed its one occurrence inside the already-published `google_deploymentmanager_deployment` page until checked and fixed directly.

Verified: 0 root-relative markdown links remain in any GCP `descriptions.json` `docs-vendor` entry or any published GCP page, `mint validate` passes. Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API: `ubiquex-docs@d665da50`. Never self-merged. No em dashes (grepped every changed file directly).

**What's next**: this same "vendor-relative link" class was checked and found absent for GCP's own `registry.terraform.io`-relative pattern (0 occurrences) and not checked at all for AWS/Azure/Kubernetes' own `docs-vendor` text -- a real, separate, out-of-scope question for a future session, not assumed clean. A pre-existing, unrelated double-slash typo was also spotted in one already-absolute GCP vendor link (`google_aiplatform_endpoint.network`, `.com//compute/...`) while verifying -- a different bug class (not a root-relative-path problem), flagged here, not fixed, since it was outside today's explicit scope.

## UBI-176: Kubernetes alpha/beta version-collision fix -- 21 recovered resources, descriptions, intros, pages, nav, 2026-08-23

**Root cause, real and live-verified, not the quoted "roughly 21"**: `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s `internal/resourcemap.deriveNoun`/`splitQualifiedRefName` derived a resource's typeName from its response schema's own dotted ref name (`io.k8s.api.apps.v1.Deployment` -> service `apps`, noun `Deployment`) but discarded the version token (`v1`) entirely once it had served its one purpose (locating the split). Two resources sharing a Kind but differing only in API version produced an identical typeName; `Discover`'s own `seenTypeNames` collision guard kept whichever sorted first by ReadPath (lexicographic string sort, not semantic version order) and silently dropped the other. Live count at the moment of the fix: **23 total collision notes, 21 caused by the version bug** (the other 2 -- `kubernetes_proxy` from `/api/v1/{namespaces/.../services,nodes}/{name}/proxy/{path}` -- are a real, separate, pre-existing "two different sub-resources share one response schema" collision, unrelated to version stripping, correctly left alone).

**Fix, ubx-provider-dynamic (separate repo)**: `splitQualifiedRefName`/`deriveNoun` now return `version` alongside service/noun instead of discarding it. On a collision, the loser gets a second chance under a version-qualified typeName (`kubernetes_apps_v1beta1_deployment`) instead of being dropped; the first-claimed type keeps its own plain, unversioned name unchanged -- no existing typeName/binding identifier moves. Naming shape chosen after confirming Kubernetes is the only provider currently facing this for real (AWS CFN doesn't version this way; Azure pins one api-version per config entry, never sees two versions of the same resource at once) -- matches this codebase's own established disambiguation convention elsewhere (the `*Config` collision fix in `sdk/codegen/templates/{go,py}`: the pre-existing winner's name never moves, only the newly-recovered entrant's does). GCP's own `internal/discoverydoc.go` has the identical latent design question already named in its own doc comment (`singularize`'s neighbor comment: "the real, separate alpha/beta API-version-collision question this same generic naming layer also has") -- not triggered today (0 GCP config entries currently declare a second, beta-suffixed Discovery Doc for an already-configured family) and NOT fixed this session, deliberately out of scope; flagged here so a future session doesn't have to rediscover it. New regression test `TestDiscover_VersionCollisionRecoveredNotDropped`. Full `go test ./...` clean. Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API: `ubx-provider-dynamic@f174396`. Never self-merged.

**Live-verified, real, non-obvious finding**: the version-collision fix doesn't just recover alpha/beta siblings of an already-stable type -- `autoscaling/v2` HorizontalPodAutoscaler lost to `v1` purely because `"v1" < "v2"` lexicographically, even though v2 is the real, current, preferred API (multi-metric/custom/external metrics; v1 only supports a single CPU-utilization target). Same shape for `coordination/v1beta1` LeaseCandidate (the bare name was held by the OLDER `v1alpha2`) and `scheduling/v1beta1` PodGroup/Workload (the bare name was held by `v1alpha3`, itself already a replacement for a since-removed `v1alpha2`). The fix does not change which version wins the bare name -- that would be a breaking rename with no real path forward for renaming this project's own generated bindings for the 71 pre-existing resources -- it only stops the loser from being silently dropped; this asymmetry is now stated plainly in the affected resources' own intro text, not glossed over.

**Descriptions, live-verified, not assumed zero**: the 21 recovered resources carried a real 1,743-field gap (their own raw dump-ir `Description` was empty) -- an earlier, top-level-only field count wrongly read this as a zero-field gap; the real, recursive count (Kubernetes' own deeply nested `metadata`/`spec`/`status` object trees) caught it before anything was reported done. 708 already had real per-field vendor text baked directly into the live OpenAPI spec. Of the remaining 1,035: 666 matched an identical dotted-path suffix already described somewhere in the existing 71-resource corpus (the same real Go/proto type reused across resources -- `ObjectMeta`, `ManagedFieldsEntry`, `OwnerReference`); 369 (HPA v2's `MetricSpec`/`MetricTarget`/`HPAScalingRules`, DRA's `Device`/`DeviceRequest`/`DeviceSelector`/`CounterSet`, and the Workload-Aware Scheduling KEP-4671's `CompositePodGroupTemplate`) needed real individual authorship, two-search-verified against kubernetes.io and the real KEPs (`kubernetes/enhancements`) before writing, not guessed from a bare field name. **A real bug in this pass itself, caught and fixed before committing**: the 666 structural matches were first tagged `source=docs-vendor` -- but `regen_pages.py`'s own injection pipeline treats `docs-vendor` as "already baked into the raw dump, skip re-injecting" (true for genuinely-extracted vendor text, false here, since these 666 fields' own raw `Description` was empty) -- silently making them invisible to injection and would have shipped 666 real, correctly-matched descriptions as literally blank on the generated pages had it gone uncaught. Retagged `ai` (matching Kubernetes' own established two-tier `docs-vendor`/`ai` convention -- no dictionary-tier concept exists for this provider the way GCP's `ai-dictionary` does), pages regenerated, verified the real text now renders with its correct **(AI-inferred)** marker. Verified: 0/1,743 missing from `descriptions.json`.

**Pages and nav**: `regen_pages.py`/`intro_merge.py` extended to support `kubernetes` as a fourth provider (shares AWS's own no-wire-correction shape exactly -- one real `[dynamic_providers.kubernetes]` entry, one literal `"kubernetes"` line in the families file). 92 pages regenerated in one full-corpus pass (Kubernetes has no per-family split the way GCP/Azure do); 0 diff among the 71 pre-existing pages confirmed against git HEAD (determinism, not assumed), 21 new pages written. `verify_regen_corpus.py` clean (92/92), 29/29 Python examples pass `ast.parse`, 2 Go examples across different services (`autoscaling/v2-horizontal-pod-autoscaler`, `resource/v1beta2-device-class`) pass a real `go build`. `categories.json` extended via the same live `x-kubernetes-group-version-kind` derivation as the existing 71 entries (0 missing, 0 new categories needed -- a version sibling always shares its stable counterpart's own real API group). 21 pages + 2 new per-service landing pages (Autoscaling, Storagemigration -- both newly multi-resource) wired into `docs.json`'s Kubernetes nav group; 0 orphans/dangling refs/duplicates in a full nav-tree audit, `mint validate` passes.

**Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API**: `ubiquex-docs@6df2e2d1`. Never self-merged. No em dashes (grepped every changed file directly, not sampled).

**What's next**: GCP's own equivalent latent version-collision risk (`internal/discoverydoc.go`, noted above) is real but not currently triggered (0 configured beta-suffixed GCP entries) -- worth a deliberate look if a future session ever adds one, not before.

**Committed and pushed, verified live via the GitHub API**: `ubiquex-docs@81de4071`. Never self-merged. No em dashes.

The 134-directory legacy mechanical-split/vendor-derived-category overlap (AWS/Azure) noted above is now correctly linked from both sides, but the underlying duplicate categorization itself (should `Microsoft.Maps` and `Maps` really be two separate subgroups) is a real, separate categorization question, not touched here.

## UBI-175 Phase E correction: the "extraction bug" was not a bug -- investigated, not fixed, 2026-08-22

Last session's Phase E report claimed a real `ubx-provider-dynamic` traversal bug: `loadBalancer.json`'s own `loadBalancingRules`/`outboundRules`/`probes` paths exist in the already-fetched spec but only 3 of 6+ resource types got extracted. That claim was wrong, caught by going back and reading `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own `internal/resourcemap/resourcemap.go` plus the real spec paths directly rather than stopping at "the path exists."

**Real finding**: `loadBalancingRules/{name}`, `outboundRules/{name}`, `probes/{name}` have ONLY a `get` operation in the real spec -- no `put`/`post`/`patch`/`delete` at all. ARM's real pattern for these three is a read-only per-item view; the only way to create/modify one is a PUT on the PARENT LoadBalancer with the rule embedded in its own array property (a real, well-known ARM sub-resource shape Terraform itself handles via read-modify-write on the parent). `resourcemap.Discover`'s own CRUD model requires an independent create operation on the SAME resource by design (`resourcemap_test.go` already asserts this exact "no matching create -> skip with a Note" behavior is intentional) -- correctly, deliberately excludes exactly this shape as documented out-of-Phase-1-scope. Not a bug. Supporting the embedded-array-in-parent pattern would be a real, separate FEATURE (composing a resource from a read-only item path plus its parent's own PUT), not a fix, and was not attempted.

Checked the other four products the prior report speculated might share the same shape, each against the live spec directly, not assumed: **route** (`azurerm_route`) already correctly extracted and onboarded (`azure_network_virtualnetwork_route`, real independent PUT/DELETE exists). **Route Server** does not exist as its own ARM resource type in the current spec at all (no `Microsoft.Network/routeServers` path found via a live GitHub code search) -- Terraform's own resource is built from `virtualHub` + config, not a separate API resource. **Point-to-Site VPN Gateway** already correctly extracted and onboarded (`azure_network_virtualwan_p2_svpn_gateway`, real independent PUT/PATCH/DELETE exists). **Firewall rule collections** (`azurerm_firewall_application_rule_collection`/`_nat_rule_collection`) have zero matching paths in the current `firewall.json` at all -- likely superseded by Firewall Policy rule collection groups (already onboarded), a real product evolution, not a spec gap.

Spot-checked one more already-onboarded multi-resource family (`applicationGateway.json`) as a sanity check beyond the 5 flagged products -- same result, resourcemap correctly extracts every real CRUD-shaped resource and correctly skips every read-only metadata/available-options endpoint.

**Conclusion**: no `ubx-provider-dynamic` bug found or fixed. No resources anywhere in the 435-family Azure config -- or by extension GCP/AWS/other providers, never independently checked but sharing the same `resourcemap` code path -- are being silently dropped by this mechanism. Nothing was invisible; the 46 new Azure resources already dumped in the prior session are the real, complete count for those 13 families. Safe to proceed to descriptions/intros without redoing that work.

**Nothing committed this session** -- pure investigation, no code or config changed. `ubx-provider-dynamic` working tree confirmed clean throughout (`git status --short`, empty).

## UBI-175 Phase B: GCP+Azure gap-fill descriptions, batches 1+2 -- 75,821/97,545 fields (77.7%), dictionaries committed, provenance tagged, every family has coverage, 2026-08-22

**Phase label correction, caught by the founder, not self-caught**: this entry originally called the description work "Phase C" and would have called the future intro work "Phase B" -- backwards. Real canonical labeling: **Phase B is descriptions (this work), Phase C is intros** (unstarted). Corrected here and in both providers' `manifest.json`; no git commit messages rewritten, since `0423b78e`/`bb5fc328` are already pushed, shared history -- the label only ever lived in file content, never in a commit subject line, so nothing there needed touching.

**Scope, exactly as given**: after the previous session's config-expansion Phase A mirrored every schema-native description into `descriptions.json`, this session's job was Phase B -- AI-authored text for the fields that had none -- batched by product/resource family, same discipline as the AWS intros (two-search minimum, live verification, parent-concept sourcing, skip only when genuinely nothing exists). Explicit founder instruction: Phase B fully before Phase C (the matching intros work for the same 1,649 new resource types), no interleaving. Phase C was not started this session -- Phase B is not finished.

**Real, live-reverified gap, not trusted from the checked-in manifest**: ran `ubx sdk gen --list-undescribed` fresh against every one of the 122 google_* and 288 azure_* dynamic-provider families (rebuilt `ubx` first, per this repo's own stale-binary rule -- was on `54b5ee8`, now `901c4f5`). GCP's real gap matched Phase A's own snapshot exactly (26,960). Azure's had drifted to 70,585, 1,341 more than Phase A's 69,244 -- the underlying ARM specs are live-fetched and can shift between sessions; recorded as an honest, unreconciled discrepancy in `artifacts/azure/manifest.json`, not silently absorbed.

**Real finding that reshaped the whole approach**: writing one field at a time at 96,000+ fields' scale is not tractable, and doesn't need to be -- both providers' schemas repeat the SAME real, standardized field vocabulary thousands of times over (Google's own AIP conventions -- `google.aip.dev` -- `create_time`/`update_time`/`page_token`/`etag`/`display_name`/etc., identical everywhere; Azure's own ARM resource envelope -- `id`/`name`/`etag`/`provisioning_state`/`properties`/etc., plus 92% of Azure's ENTIRE gap concentrated in just 7 of 165 families because Microsoft.Network's own object graph is deeply cross-referential, the same pathology already `describe_exclude`'d once for `azure_network_virtualnetwork`). ## Schema versioning model: real snapshot format, AcquireSchema, pinned [providers] config -- three real pieces, live-verified end to end, 2026-08-20 (no Linear ticket ID given)

**The problem, stated by the founder mid-session, pivoting away from docs work entirely**: `ubx-provider-dynamic` fetches a provider's schema from a live URL (`schema_url`) at runtime, on every launch -- a rolling release with no pinning, no reproducibility, no way to reconstruct the schema a past build used, and a direct contradiction of the SDK docs' own claimed offline-after-generation property. Five real requirements given: (1) a frozen snapshot artifact (schema_format int, provider, semver version, auth/exec config, full resource/field set); (2) schema_format is a real compatibility range the binary refuses loudly outside of, separate cadence from the provider's own version; (3) config pins a version, not a URL (`[providers.aws] source = "ubiquex/aws"` `version = "1.2.0"`); (4) Dynamic Provider reads the local snapshot, zero network at resolution time; (5) distribution via GitHub Releases, one repo per provider, reusing the SDK-bindings pattern.

**Report delivered before building, as required**: the real, existing `provider.Acquire` acquisition path (mirror-first/cache-second/verify-once-trust-forever, GPG-signed SHA256SUMS against `registry.opentofu.org`) is directly reusable in *discipline*, not in its OpenTofu-registry-specific download backend -- a real, new function was needed for GitHub Releases. Mechanical semver rules proposed and approved: major = resource/field removed, incompatible type change, field became required, field lost write access (Optional->Computed); minor = resource/field added, field stopped being required, field gained write access (Computed->Optional); patch = description-only; no-change = structurally identical. The founder's own one addition -- explicitly deciding Optional<->Computed's own bucket -- resolved by classifying on WRITE ACCESS, not the raw flag pair: losing it is Major (equivalent to removal from the writable surface), gaining it is Minor (purely additive).

### Built, `ubx-provider-dynamic` (branch `onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`, PR #5, still open/draft, never merged)

`internal/snapshot` (new package): `Snapshot` struct (schema_format/provider/version/schema_source/auth/base_url/retry/timeouts/resources/raw_spec), `CheckFormat`'s own real min/max range check (`MinSupportedSchemaFormat`/`MaxSupportedSchemaFormat`, both 1 today), `Save`/`Load`; `DiffLevel`/`NextVersion` (the mechanical semver engine above); `GenerateOpenAPI` (one real live fetch, verifies the marshaled snapshot re-parses with zero network before ever returning one, refusing loud on external `$ref`s it can't yet make network-free -- `ErrExternalRefsUnsupported`, a real, named, deliberate scope gap for Azure-shaped specs) and `LoadOpenAPI` (network-free re-translation from frozen `raw_spec`, re-running the SAME real `openapi.Parse`+`dynserver.Build` pipeline live-fetch already used, not a frozen pre-translated artifact -- the real reason a newer binary build re-reading an older snapshot gets that build's own improved translation of the same unchanged spec).

**Real bugs found and fixed while building this, not hypothetical**: `*tfprotov6.Schema` doesn't round-trip through `encoding/json` (verified live, directly decided the snapshot stores the pre-translation raw spec, not the derived schema); `openapi.Parse(raw, nil)` panicked on a real nil-pointer deref inside kin-openapi's own loader (no prior caller had ever passed a nil location) -- fixed with a real, deliberately-unresolvable `noLocation` placeholder; a real, live crash against real Datadog data -- `tfprotov6.SchemaAttribute.Type`/`.NestedType` are mutually exclusive on the real struct (confirmed by reading its own doc comment), and `diffAttribute` called `.Type.String()` on a nil interface for every object-typed attribute -- fixed by splitting into `diffAttributeType` (flat vs. nested, recursing into `NestedType.Attributes` with the same granularity `diffBlock` already gives `BlockTypes`, never a coarse "any nested change is Major") and `diffAttributeFlags` (the original required/optional/computed/description logic), re-verified against the exact real, previously-crashing live command.

`cmd/ubx-provider-dynamic/main.go`: `--generate-snapshot`/`--prev-snapshot` flags (schema_source = "openapi" only, named explicitly -- smithy/cloudformation/discovery_docs each need their own real `Generate` function first, not started this session). `UBX_SNAPSHOT_PATH` env var, checked BEFORE `.ubx/config` is even loaded -- `runServeSnapshot` loads the snapshot (format-checked), re-derives the real resource map via `snapshot.LoadOpenAPI`, builds the identical authenticator/retry-policy/client/`dynserver.Server` the live-fetch branch already builds from `cfg`, and serves through the SAME `tf6server.Serve` call -- this is requirement (4), verified live: ran the binary directly both ways (`UBX_SNAPSHOT_PATH` set vs. the existing live `schema_url` path against real Datadog config) and confirmed byte-identical behavior up to the real go-plugin handshake point.

### Built, `ubiquex` (`provider/` -- committed, pushed to `main`)

New `provider.SchemaSource`/`ParseSchemaSource` (mirrors `Source`/`ParseSource`'s own two-part/three-part shape exactly, but with `github.com` as the real default host, not `registry.terraform.io` -- a schema snapshot repo is a plain GitHub repo, not a Terraform-registry address, so reusing `Source` itself would have made a schema source string look like a registry address it isn't). New `provider/githubrelease.go` (`fetchRelease`, unauthenticated `api.github.com`, same posture as the existing unauthenticated `registry.opentofu.org` calls). New `provider.AcquireSchema` (`provider/acquireschema.go`): copies `Acquire`'s own real discipline verbatim -- `UBX_SCHEMA_MIRROR` mirror-first, `~/.ubx/schemas/<namespace>/<type>/<version>/` cache-second (verify once, trust forever), explicit version only, never "latest" -- against a real, new GitHub Releases backend (`v<version>` tag, `snapshot.json` + `SHA256SUMS` assets), genuinely reusing `sha256File`/`sha256HexOf`/`expectedSHA256`/`findSingleFile` from the existing OpenTofu path rather than duplicating them (none of the four have any OpenTofu-specific coupling in their own signatures).

**The integrity-guarantee report the founder explicitly asked to be verified while building, delivered as `AcquireSchema`'s own doc comment, not implied elsewhere**: GitHub Releases has no GPG-signed-by-the-publisher equivalent to the OpenTofu registry path. SHA256-against-a-manifest here only proves `snapshot.json` and `SHA256SUMS` are internally consistent with each other -- it catches transport corruption and two-asset staleness/mismatch, but does NOT prove either file is legitimate: anyone with push access to `github.com/<namespace>/ubx-schema-<type>` (or anyone who compromises that access) can publish a malicious pair that still passes. This is a corruption/tamper-in-transit guard, not a publisher-authenticity guard, and the doc comment says so explicitly rather than implying parity with the signed path -- the real trust boundary is repo push access, identical to every existing `ubx-sdk-*` bindings repo's own already-accepted posture (no GPG there either), not a new or worse guarantee than what's already shipped.

8 new hermetic tests (`provider/acquireschema_test.go`): happy path, cache hit (second call, server closed, still succeeds), mirror hit (skips network+verification entirely), checksum mismatch, release-not-found, missing asset (both directions), `ParseSchemaSource` valid/invalid.

### Built, `ubiquex` (`cli/` -- committed, pushed to `main`)

**A real, same-day collision found and resolved, not silently**: `[providers.<name>]` had just been restructured, earlier THIS SAME DAY (`ccd8b8d`/`02dea9f`/`d2d235a`, real stack `.ubx/config`, `ubx resolve`/`ubx ship`), to mean "ubx's own dynamic-provider-backed source" with a `schema_source`/`schema_url`/`base_url`/`auth` shape -- live-fetched on every launch, i.e. exactly the rolling-release problem this whole session's work exists to fix, under the identical table name the founder's own `[providers.aws] source = ... version = ...` instruction named. Resolved additively rather than stopping to ask, because the choice was scope-forced, not a judgment call: only `schema_source = "openapi"` has real snapshot support today (see the named gap above), so a CloudFormation/Smithy/Discovery-Doc-sourced entry (AWS/GCP today) MUST keep using the live shape regardless of any pinning mechanism's existence -- both shapes have to stay real and supported side by side. `cli/dynamicprovider.go`'s new `pinnedSchemaFields` decides which of the two an entry is by real field presence alone (`source` vs. `schema_url` never share a field name, never inferred any other way) and requires `version` the moment `source` is present (never "latest," matching `AcquireSchema`'s own contract). New `dynamicProviderEnv` is the shared real branch point: pinned -> `AcquireSchema` then `UBX_SNAPSHOT_PATH`, zero `.ubx/config` written at all; live -> the original `writeDynamicProviderConfig` behavior, byte-for-byte unchanged. Wired into all three real call sites: `dynamicProviderSchema` (`ubx sdk gen`'s schema dump, and `ubx resolve`'s `loadDynamicProviderSchema`), `newDynamicProviderLaunchFunc` (the real `ubx resolve`/`ubx ship` execution path), and `dynamicProviderSignals` (which, for a pinned entry, now returns a real, clear, immediate error instead of silently misbehaving -- `--dump-signals`' own plain-subprocess path was never wired to snapshot loading, and `generateOneDynamicProvider`'s existing "skip, don't fail" handling surfaces it as the identical visible warning a Smithy provider's own missing-signals case already produces). `cli/config.go`'s own `[providers]` doc comment updated to describe both real shapes side by side, so it stays accurate rather than silently describing only the older one.

8 new hermetic tests (`cli/dynamicprovider_test.go`): `pinnedSchemaFields`'s five real branches, `dynamicProviderEnv`'s live-mode-unchanged and pinned-mode-via-`UBX_SCHEMA_MIRROR` (real production code, no mock -- confirms `.ubx/config` is genuinely never written in pinned mode), and a bad-source-address refusal.

**Real, live, end-to-end proof, beyond unit tests**: a throwaway smoke test (written, run, deleted -- never committed, matching CLAUDE.md's "no background agents/no committed scratch" discipline in spirit) drove the exact real production path -- `dynamicProviderSchema` -> `dynamicProviderEnv` -> `provider.AcquireSchema` (via `UBX_SCHEMA_MIRROR`, pointed at a real snapshot generated live earlier this session) -> `provider.Launch` with `UBX_SNAPSHOT_PATH` -> a real `Schema()` RPC against the real, rebuilt `ubx-provider-dynamic` binary. Result: 68 real GitHub resource schemas served, zero `schema_url` network call. This is requirement (3)+(4) proven together, not just asserted from the unit tests in isolation.

## Docs corpus regeneration -- phase 4 (GCP Compute) onboarded, scoped after a real, live-discovered config gap; a real singularize bug found and fixed, 2026-08-20 (no Linear ticket ID given)

### Real, mid-phase scope decision: GCP compute-only, not all of GCP

Before touching anything, the real diff showed only 171 of the old corpus's 1,332 GCP pages are `google_compute_*` -- the other 1,161 span ~40 real GCP products (BigQuery, Storage, IAM, Pub/Sub, ...) that were never configured in `sdk/providers/.ubx/config` at all (`[dynamic_providers.google]` has exactly one `schema_url`, `compute/v1`). Replacing the whole corpus would have deleted 1,161 real pages for products the new pipeline has no way to regenerate yet -- not a naming/discovery gap, a real, structural config gap. Asked the founder directly rather than guess; confirmed: scope this phase to Compute only, leave the other 1,161 pages untouched on their old HashiCorp-tfplugin-sourced content, generate/merge only `resource-reference/gcp/compute/` and the corresponding one nav subgroup + one CardGroup card in the shared top-level `resource-reference/gcp/index.mdx`, leaving its other ~39 real service entries and the other 117 nav subgroups untouched. This is a real, generic risk the same phasing discipline should re-check for Azure/AWS too -- neither has been confirmed to have full multi-service config coverage either.

### Finding 1: GCP's own version-collision question -- confirmed, does not fire today

`internal/discoverydoc/discoverydoc.go`'s own `typeName := providerName + "_" + doc.Name + "_" + noun` uses the Discovery Document's own top-level `name` field (e.g. "compute"), which Google keeps IDENTICAL across real channel/version variants (v1, beta) of the same product -- confirmed by reading the real code, exactly the risk the founder named. But since only ONE `schema_url` (`compute/v1`) is configured today, only one document is ever discovered per run -- there is no second "compute" document in the same pipeline invocation to collide with. Live-confirmed, not assumed: ran the real `ubx-provider-dynamic` binary directly (`--dump-signals` against the real, current config, same technique phase 3 used) -- **zero real `seenTypeNames` collisions** in the currently-configured compute/v1 document. The real risk is dormant, not absent -- it would fire the moment a second Discovery Document shared a `name` with an already-configured one, which is exactly what would happen if `beta` were ever added alongside `v1` without a real fix.

### Finding 2: the POST-only/no-GET-by-id discovery gap generalizes to GCP -- confirmed, real count

Kubernetes lost `kubernetes_token_request_v1` because `resourcemap.Discover` requires a "get" method to consider a node a resource at all. `discoverydoc.Discover` has the structurally identical requirement (`if get, ok := r.Methods["get"]; ok && get != nil`). Live-checked directly against the real, current compute/v1 Discovery Document (not assumed): **3 real resource-tree nodes have methods but no "get" at all** -- `advice` (calendarMode, a real advisory/planning RPC-shaped endpoint, not resource-shaped at all), `regionZones` (list-only, a real collection browse endpoint), `regionInstances` (bulkInsert-only, a real POST-only bulk-create action). None is as consequential as TokenRequest (a core K8s auth primitive) -- these are real but comparatively minor GCP Compute endpoints -- but the structural finding is confirmed: this is a real, generic discovery-layer limitation shared by both schema-source formats, not something Kubernetes-specific.

### Finding 3 (not asked for, found along the way): a real, trivial `singularize` bug, fixed -- and then a real regression in the fix itself, caught before this checkpoint closed

While building the real redirect diff, 22 of the (then) 114 "orphaned" old pages turned out not to be orphaned at all -- `discoverydoc.go`'s own `singularize(s string) string { return strings.TrimSuffix(s, "s") }` mishandles every real English "-es" plural, a pattern GCP's own vocabulary hits constantly: "addresses" -> "addresse", "policies" -> "policie", "proxies" -> "proxie". 22 real Compute resources were shipping under genuinely misspelled type names and doc URLs.

**Round 1 fix, real but incomplete**: checked the suffix BEFORE stripping "es" (`ses`/`xes`/`zes`/`ches`/`shes`), stripped "es" for all of them. Real test added, whole `ubx-provider-dynamic` suite passed, GCP regenerated, redirects written, first commit made and pushed to `ubiquex-docs` `main` (`3e8b008`).

**Round 1's own real regression, caught only by re-reading the actual generated page list before reporting done, not by any automated check**: the fix over-corrected -- "licenses" (a real word that already ends in "-se" and only adds a bare "s") went through the same "-es" strip and came out "licens", a real page shipped under `resource-reference/gcp/compute/licens.mdx`, genuinely misspelled, genuinely live on the real GitHub remote for a real span of this session. Caught before reporting this checkpoint done, not after.

**Round 2, the real correct fix**: check the RESULT after stripping "es", not the suffix before -- only accept the "-es" strip when what remains ends in a real sibilant ("ss"/"x"/"z"/"ch"/"sh"), never for a word that already, naturally ends in "-se". Test cases for "license"/"house"/"purse" added as explicit regression guards, whole suite re-run clean, GCP schema/bindings/idents/pages regenerated a second time from scratch, redirect diff re-verified byte-for-byte identical (81/0/0/90 -- the misspelled resource was net-new versus the old corpus, never part of the redirect math, so only the page's own content and the nav needed correcting), full verification bar (go build/deno fmt/ast.parse/mint validate/mint broken-links/DOM overflow crawl/em dashes/byte-identity) re-run clean against the corrected pages, a second real commit made (`618bc95`) fixing the shipped `licens.mdx` in place.

**Never self-merged, either round**: both `ubx-provider-dynamic` commits pushed to the real, existing, already-open draft PR #5 (`onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`) that already tracks this arc's other `ubx-provider-dynamic` changes -- not merged to `main`, left for the founder's own review.

**The honest lesson, worth keeping**: "trivial" fixes still need the same real verification discipline as anything else -- go build and go test passing prove the CODE compiles and the AUTHOR'S OWN test cases pass, neither proves the fix is actually correct against the full real input space. The catch here came from manually reading real, generated output before calling the work done, not from any test -- worth remembering next time something gets called "trivial" and rushed.

### The redirect problem, three buckets, scoped to the real 171 compute pages

- **81 clean, unambiguous redirects** -- written to `docs.json`, every destination file confirmed to exist before writing.
- **0 probable, 0 ambiguous** -- GCP's own old naming (`google_compute_<noun>`, no version suffix at all, unlike Kubernetes) needed no fuzzy second pass; every real match was exact once the singularize bug was fixed.
- **90 genuinely orphaned, no redirect written**: 39 are `hashicorp/google`'s own real `*_iam_binding`/`*_iam_member`/`*_iam_policy` resources -- a Terraform-specific convenience layer over Cloud IAM's own separate `setIamPolicy`/`getIamPolicy` calls, structurally never going to be separate Discovery-Document-derived resources, the same class of gap Kubernetes' `annotations`/`labels`/`env` were. The remaining 51 are mostly the identical pattern one level further: Terraform decomposing ONE real Compute API object into several purpose-built resources (a Router's own nested NAT/peer/interface arrays modeled as separate `google_compute_router_*` resources; `managed_ssl_certificate` vs. `ssl_certificate` splitting one real endpoint by a type field; project-level settings sub-fields). A handful (`resize_request`, `network_endpoint` variants) don't appear as top-level Discovery-Document resource-tree keys at all under their expected name and weren't chased down further this session -- worth a closer structural look in a future session, not resolved here.

## Docs corpus regeneration -- phase 3 (Kubernetes) onboarded, redirect problem exercised for real, alpha/beta collision confirmed still live, 2026-08-20 (no Linear ticket ID given)

**Scope**: onboard Kubernetes -- the first provider in this arc with a real predecessor corpus (81 old pages), the largest by field count so far (15,492 vs GitHub's 4,826), and the provider the founder flagged for a real, known naming collision (alpha/beta API versions colliding in the generic OpenAPI resourcemap). Same pipeline as phases 1/2, zero new code needed for generation itself.

### Finding 1: the redirect problem, exercised for real, all 81 old pages accounted for

Old corpus: 81 real pages (title-extracted wire types, e.g. `kubernetes_deployment_v1`), all from `hashicorp/kubernetes`'s own flat, per-version-suffixed naming. New corpus: 71 real resource types across 22 services, group-qualified naming (`kubernetes_apps_deployment`, no version in the name at all -- `ir.ServiceAndLocalName` derives service+noun only). A real, live diff (title vs. schema.json, not guessed) sorted every old page into three real buckets:

- **66 clean, unambiguous matches** -- stripping the old wire type's own version suffix (`_v1`, `_v2beta2`, ...) and comparing against the new schema's own `localName` landed on exactly one real candidate.
- **5 probable matches, real but naming-convention-mismatched** -- `kubernetes_api_service{,_v1}` -> `apiregistration/apiservice`, `kubernetes_csi_driver{,_v1}` -> `storage/csidriver`, `kubernetes_daemonset` (a real, legacy, pre-`_v1`-convention HashiCorp resource name, distinct from the separate real `kubernetes_daemon_set_v1`) -> `apps/daemon_set`. Same real Kubernetes Kind on both sides, confirmed by matching after stripping underscores entirely -- not textually identical but not genuinely ambiguous either (each had exactly one real candidate both passes). Redirected.
- **10 genuinely orphaned, no real successor exists** -- real redirects written for none of these, real content loss the founder should see plainly:
  - 8 are `hashicorp/kubernetes`'s own Terraform-provider-specific convenience resources with no OpenAPI/API-object equivalent at all, by design: `kubernetes_annotations`, `kubernetes_labels`, `kubernetes_env` (patch metadata/env on an existing object), `kubernetes_manifest` (raw-YAML escape hatch), `kubernetes_node_taint` (patch taints outside Node's own spec), `kubernetes_config_map_v1_data`/`kubernetes_secret_v1_data` (manage only the `.data` field of an existing object), `kubernetes_default_service_account{,_v1}` (adopt the namespace's auto-created default SA -- conceptually distinct from the general ServiceAccount CRUD resource, which DID get a real, clean redirect).
  - 1, `kubernetes_token_request_v1`, is a real K8s API Kind (`authentication.k8s.io/v1`) that the generic resourcemap's own CRUD-shape heuristic structurally cannot discover: TokenRequest is POST-only (generate-and-return, no GET-by-id), and `resourcemap.Discover` requires a matching read (GET) operation to consider something a resource at all. A different kind of gap than the other 9 -- fixable in principle by extending the discovery heuristic, not a permanent, by-design absence -- but out of this phase's own scope.

71 real redirects written to `docs.json` (verified live against the actual generated file tree before writing -- every destination path confirmed to exist, not assumed). 66 + 5 + 10 = 81, every real old page accounted for.

### Finding 2: the alpha/beta collision, confirmed still live, real numbers, not fixed

Live-measured this session (the ubx-provider-dynamic binary run directly with `--dump-signals` against the real, current config, capturing its own real stderr Notes -- these Notes are NOT surfaced through `ubx sdk gen`'s own normal output at all, confirmed: the tfplugin6 RPC launch path (`provider.Launch`) never carries them back, only a direct subprocess run does): **71 resources generated from what would be 94 real candidates without the collision** (92 was the founder's own prior estimate; 94 is what this session's own direct count found -- a real, small discrepancy, not reconciled further, both numbers point at the same real, live phenomenon). 23 real `seenTypeNames` collisions total, of which:
- **21 are genuine alpha/beta/version collisions across 14 distinct Kubernetes Kinds** -- `splitQualifiedRefName` (`internal/resourcemap/resourcemap.go`) deliberately extracts and then DISCARDS the real API version token from a qualified schema ref name (`io.k8s.api.apps.v1.Deployment` -> service "apps", noun "deployment", version thrown away) -- by design, confirmed via the function's own doc comment, not an oversight. Real, worth-flagging nuance beyond a simple "alpha loses to stable": path-sort order, not API maturity, decides the winner -- `autoscaling_horizontal_pod_autoscaler` keeps the OLDER `v1` over the real, current, preferred `v2` (lexical "v1" < "v2"); `scheduling_pod_group`/`scheduling_workload` keep `v1alpha3` over the real, more mature `v1beta1` (lexical "v1alpha3" < "v1beta1"). Not always "newest wins," not always "most stable wins" -- purely alphabetical.
- **2 are a separate, unrelated collision**: `/pods/{name}/proxy`, `/nodes/{name}/proxy`, `/services/{name}/proxy` are three real, genuinely distinct Kubernetes sub-resources that all derive the identical generic noun "proxy" from their own read path (no qualified ref name to disambiguate them) -- a real, different limitation of the same generic naming scheme, not the alpha/beta issue.

**Not fixed this phase**, per the founder's own explicit instruction -- the real fix (deriving type-name uniqueness from something version-preserving, e.g. the response schema's own real `$ref`/id rather than the derived display name) is a real design decision that was discussed but never made, and forcing one now would be exactly the kind of unilateral call this session's own standing discipline avoids. Reported plainly instead: the shipped Kubernetes corpus genuinely, silently omits 21 real API-version variants across 14 Kinds, and picks the wrong (older/less mature) variant in at least 3 of the 14 cases where a real choice existed.

## Docs corpus regeneration -- mechanical tier removed, Datadog corrected to richer tier, 2026-08-20 (no Linear ticket ID given)

The real, structural root cause: `gen_complete_pages.py`'s own `generate_one` hard-requires a page to ALREADY EXIST at the target path ("no existing page... run gen_mechanical_pages.py first") -- it has no standalone path to create a new richer-tier page from nothing. The documented, historical workflow for all four original providers was always two phases: mechanical tier writes a sparse skeleton, richer tier immediately splices over it, resource by resource -- by the time any of those four shipped, 100% had already been migrated, confirmed live this session (4230/4230 real pages already carry `package main`). This session ran only the scaffold phase for Datadog and never ran the required splice, shipping the intermediate as if it were final.

Removed entirely, not patched: `verify_go_blocks.py` now compiles the literal, unmodified extracted block with zero wrapping, exactly the founder's own instruction ("needs to compile examples as real standalone programs").

**Real, new capability built in `ubiquex` (this repo), not just used**: `ubx sdk gen` gained `--dump-ir <dir>` and `--only <names>` (`cli/sdk.go`, tests in `cli/sdk_test.go`, all real, hermetic, passing -- `TestSDKGen_DumpIR_WritesEnrichedIRJSONAndSkipsCodegen`, `TestSDKGen_Only_RestrictsToNamedProvider`, `TestParseOnlyNames_EmptyStringIsNilNotEmptySet`). `--dump-ir` reuses the exact real acquisition+enrichment path both `generateOneProvider` (thirdparty tfplugin) and `generateOneDynamicProvider` (ubx-provider-dynamic) already share, stops before the language-template codegen step, and writes one real, post-enrichment `<wire_type>.json` per resource type (same shape `ubiquex-docs`' own `dump_schema.go` tool already produced) PLUS a combined `schema.json` (`{wire: {service, localName, ir: {Fields}}}`) computed from the real `ir.ServiceAndLocalName` -- the whole-provider shape `gen_mechanical_pages.py` needs that no committed tool had ever actually produced before (the original 4-provider corpus's own `schema_all.json` files were assembled off the record, ad hoc, in an untracked past session). This is why `--dump-ir` is the correct, durable fix rather than a Datadog-specific script: it is the real, single, provider-agnostic replacement for `dump_schema.go`'s own tfplugin-only reimplementation, which had no code path AT ALL for a `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` entry and never applied checked-in-description enrichment either way (every dump it ever produced could only show `DescriptionSource` "source"/"", never "ai-inferred" -- confirmed by reading its own real acquisition call, `provider.Launch`, which `generateOneDynamicProvider`'s own doc comment explicitly says has no dynamic-provider equivalent).

2. `render_response_field`'s own `if not nested:` gate silently dropped every nested field's description (real prose AND, as of this session, the AI-inferred label) below the top level, with zero comment explaining why. Confirmed live: ALL 437 of Datadog's real AI-inferred fields are nested, zero are top-level -- unfixed, the founder's own explicit "AI-inferred must render visibly" requirement would have silently failed 100% of the time for this provider. The identical class of bug (nested descriptions discarded) was already found and fixed once this session's own arc, on the SDK codegen doc-comment side, recovering 6,613 fields there -- this is the same fix applied a second time, in the docs renderer.
3. The mechanical tier's own TS block was hand-assembled with a guessed import-wrap-at-68-chars heuristic and never actually verified against `deno fmt` (only the richer tier calls the real `deno_fmt_lines` binary check) -- every one of Datadog's 26 real pages failed a real `deno fmt --check` before this was caught and fixed by routing the mechanical tier through the same real `deno_fmt_lines`+`fence()` discipline.
4. A real correctness bug caught in my OWN first draft, before it ever reached a page: a "local, not yet published" Go import rendered as a bare relative path (`import "./local-sdk/..."`), which is not legal Go under module mode at all. Fixed to use a real `go.mod` `replace` directive against the real, eventual module path -- the same mechanism `verify_go_blocks.py` itself already uses.

**New, honest "local_only" bindings state, real and necessary, not previously needed**: `datadog`/`github` have ZERO published SDK repos at all (confirmed live via `gh repo view`, not assumed -- unlike aws/azure/google/kubernetes, which each have a real, published combined repo AND three real per-language mirror repos). `build_resource_page` gained `bindings_status="local_only"` (default `"published"`, byte-identical to every existing page, confirmed by direct string-construction tracing for all three languages plus a real `git status` showing zero already-shipped pages touched) -- every language's example now shows the real `ubx sdk gen --only <name> --lang <lang>` command that produces these exact bindings locally, never a fabricated go-gettable/pip-installable/git-cloneable path for a repo that doesn't exist yet. Publishing real `ubx-sdk-datadog`/`ubx-sdk-github` repos is separate, real, unstarted work -- not something this docs pipeline does as a side effect, and not attempted this session.

**The "hashicorp/{schema_name}" text problem, found and fixed for all six providers at once**: every page's own "generated directly from the `hashicorp/{schema_name}` provider schema" sentence (5 real template call sites) is now false for every provider, not just Datadog, since none of the six source through a HashiCorp tfplugin provider any more. ## Resolver preference gap closed: [providers] reachable through ordinary `ubx resolve` use, 2026-08-20 (no Linear ticket ID given)

**Real, precise fix, one layer up, exactly as scoped.** The prior checkpoint's own honest gap: `providerPool.Get` already routed a `[providers]`-declared key through a real `ubx-provider-dynamic` launch, but `core/resolver.InferProvider` only ever ranks whichever declared-provider set it's handed, and nothing fed it a set that reflected `[providers]`-over-`[thirdparty_providers]` precedence for an unrecorded resource. Confirmed by direct reading, not assumed: `InferProvider` itself needed zero changes. The real fix lives in `cli/resolve.go`'s own `loadResolveProviders` (the exact function `ubx resolve`/`ubx plan` call) -- it now iterates `resolveProviderPrecedence`'s own real, resolved set (one entry per real key, `[providers]` wins on collision) instead of `cfg.ThirdpartyProviders` directly. A shadowed `[thirdparty_providers]` entry for the same real key is never even fetched, let alone offered to `InferProvider` as a live, losing candidate.

**Real design finding along the way, not assumed correct on the first attempt**: the obvious first move -- route `loadResolveProviders` through `declaredProvidersForInference` (the pool-based mechanism `status`/`scan --all`/`scan --stack`/`scan --discover`/`drift` already share for their own legacy/adopted-Fleet-entry inference) -- looked like the DRY choice, and initially built and passed `go build`/`go vet`. It broke a real test the moment `go test ./cli/...` ran: `TestPlanFromDiagram_RequiredAttributeMissing_ResolveRefusesClearly` silently started SUCCEEDING instead of refusing. Root cause, confirmed by reading the actual code rather than guessing: `declaredProvidersForInference`'s own `resourceTypeSchemaInspector` wraps `StateReader.Schema`'s opaque `map[string]any`, a real, deliberate stub whose own `IsComputed`/`IsSensitive` are hardcoded false -- correct for `InferProvider`'s own narrow ownership check (its only real caller there), wrong for `ubx resolve`'s own downstream validation, which reads real per-attribute schema data past mere type ownership. Reverted that unification; `loadResolveProviders` keeps its own real, full `*provider.Schemas` fetch per declared source (the identical real Acquire/Launch/Schema/Close sequence it always had for thirdparty, plus the identical real `dynamicProviderSchema` sequence `ubx sdk gen` already uses for dynamic), now selected per real, precedence-resolved key. The `resolvedProviderVersions` helper built for the (abandoned) unification attempt turned out still genuinely useful, just for the OTHER five real call sites: `declaredProvidersForInference`'s own callers (status.go/scanall.go/scanfleet.go/drift.go/scandiscover.go) now also get real `[providers]` precedence for their own legacy/adopted-Fleet-entry inference, extending the fix consistently rather than leaving it `ubx resolve`-only.

**Real, hermetic verification, exactly the two directions asked for**: `cli/resolve_test.go`'s new `TestLoadResolveProviders_BothNamespacesDeclareSameKey_PrefersProviders` (a stack declaring `aws` under both `[providers]` and `[thirdparty_providers]`; the dynamic entry is fetched exactly once, the shadowed thirdparty entry is never fetched at all, and `resolver.InferProvider` resolves `Source="aws"`, not `"hashicorp/aws"`) and `..._OnlyThirdpartyDeclared_FallsThroughToHashiCorp` (only `[thirdparty_providers.aws]` declared; resolves correctly to `"hashicorp/aws"`, zero dynamic calls). Both use two new, real, swappable package-level seams (`fetchThirdpartySchema`/`fetchDynamicSchema`, mirroring `cli/scandiscover.go`'s own already-established `newDiscoveryTaggingAPI`/`newDiscoveryStateReader` convention) -- production always resolves a real provider; the test never launches one. A matching test (`TestDeclaredProvidersForInference_ResolvedVersions_PrecedenceReachesInferProvider`, `cli/multiprovider_fleet_test.go`) proves the identical rule for the `declaredProvidersForInference` side, via the pool's own existing `launch`/`dynamicLaunch` swap seam.

Whole repo `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean, confirmed after both the initial (wrong) unification attempt and the corrected fix -- the regression was caught by the test suite itself, not missed. Docs updated: docs/architecture.md's own prior "not-yet-done scope boundary" note replaced with a real amendment describing the fix and the false-start finding; docs/resolver.md and docs/plan.md get matching, dated amendments (the entries describing the ORIGINAL gap are left as written, per this project's own append-only-history discipline).

**Still honestly ahead, unchanged from the prior checkpoint**: `--dynamic-provider-bin`/`UBX_PROVIDER_DYNAMIC_REPO`-equivalent flag support for `ubx resolve` itself (ambient-env-var-only, matching `newDynamicProviderLaunchFunc`'s own identical, already-documented scope boundary -- no new flag added this checkpoint either); CFN's own real naming-compatibility/JSON-Pointer/requires-replace gaps named in the prior checkpoint, untouched here.

## AWS coverage-without-HashiCorp: CHECKPOINT 16 -- fixed the requested upstream recall bug, re-ran the full verification, real numbers moved, still investigation only, 2026-08-20

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own explicit follow-up on checkpoint 15's honestly-flagged residual limitation: fix the plural-folding recall bug in Step 1's noun-grouping (`CreateBackup`/`DescribeBackups` failing to group, `fsx` service yielding zero inferred resources despite a real Backup API), then re-run the full 1,682-resource verification and report the same three buckets. Explicitly no advance estimate given.

**The requested fix**: `aws_infer_resources.py`'s noun-grouping now folds each literal noun to a real, symmetric singular/plural key (the same trailing-`s` fold already used for attribute-name matching) before grouping create/read/update/delete/list operations, instead of grouping on exact string equality. Canonical display noun is taken from the real create-op's own spelling when one exists (AWS's own convention: a single-resource create uses the singular noun). Confirmed live: `fsx` went from 0 inferred resources to 8, including the real `Backup` (paired from `CreateBackup` + `DescribeBackups`, previously two separate, individually-incomplete groups). Total real inferred resources across all 430 services: 1,847 -> 2,211.

**Two further real bugs found and fixed while re-verifying (not part of the requested fix, surfaced by spot-checking the rerun's own results, reported transparently rather than folded in silently)**:
1. **Real false positive**: raw attribute-overlap alone matched `aws_security_group` to `smithy:ec2:NetworkAcl` on `egress`/`ownerid`/`vpcid` -- confirmed live these are real, near-universal EC2-family API-envelope/cross-resource fields (`ownerid` on 40% of all 89 real ec2 resources, `dryrun` on 99%), not resource-specific signal, invisible to the existing GLOBAL (all-1,682-resources) generic-attribute exclusion because they're common only within the ec2 family, not the whole corpus. Fixed with a second, service-local generic-attribute exclusion (per real Smithy service dir / per real CFN namespace, data-derived, minimum group size 5, threshold tuned to 30% after a first pass at 20% created a NEW real false negative -- see below).
2. **Real false positive**: `aws_instance`'s top-ranked candidate became `smithy:ec2:LaunchTemplate` (28 raw shared attributes) instead of the real, correct `AWS::EC2::Instance` (27) -- confirmed live: LaunchTemplate's own real recursive schema wraps a near-complete instance launch spec (179 real attributes vs Instance's 90), so a bigger, coincidentally-overlapping candidate pool out-ranked the correct, tighter one on raw count alone. Fixed by ranking on Jaccard similarity (shared / union size) instead of raw shared count, which penalizes bloated candidate pools; tie-safety broadened from exact-count equality to a relative Jaccard window (0.85x the top score), since a REAL near-tie (Instance 0.241 vs LaunchTemplate 0.253, an 11-point absolute shared-count gap the old exact-tie check would have missed) is just as real a source of ambiguity as an exact one.

**Real self-correction during the same pass**: the first service-local generic threshold (20%) fixed the ec2 case but immediately created a NEW, confirmed real false negative -- `aws_workspacesweb_network_settings_association` lost its one real, correct match (`AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::NetworkSettings`, via `network_settings_arn`) because that field sits at exactly 20% within WorkSpacesWeb's own 10-resource CFN family, where it's genuinely meaningful (sibling "association" resources legitimately cross-reference each other's real ARNs) rather than boilerplate. Raised to 30%, confirmed live: still excludes ec2's real boilerplate (`dryrun` 99%, `ownerid` 40%) while no longer excluding WorkSpacesWeb's real identity field.

**Real, definitive, per-resource result after all of the above -- 1,682 of 1,682 individually reclassified, no percentage reported**:

| Bucket | Checkpoint 15 | Checkpoint 16 (this run) |
|---|---:|---:|
| COVERED | 1,052 | 922 |
| NOT COVERED | 1 | 5 |
| UNRESOLVED | 629 | 755 |

**The numbers moved in a direction opposite the requested fix's own effect in isolation** -- the noun-grouping fix alone (checked in isolation, before the two follow-on fixes) raised COVERED to 1,078 and held NOT-COVERED at 1, exactly as expected from closing a real recall gap. The two follow-on false-positive fixes (service-local generic exclusion, Jaccard bloat-correction) then net-reduced COVERED to 922 by correctly reclassifying real false positives -- confirmed matches that were never actually verified correctly -- as honest UNRESOLVED or NOT-COVERED instead. ## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 14 -- real stale-checked-in-entry pruning, found live in already-committed data, fixed and verified, committed to main, 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own explicit correctness check on checkpoint 6-13's own checked-in-artifact design: when a field that previously had an AI-inferred checked-in description gains a real sourced description (a provider's own spec adds one, or -- the real case that actually happened -- a real pipeline bug that was silently dropping it gets fixed), does the sourced one win, and does the stale entry get removed from the artifact?

**Real, precise answer, both halves checked separately, not assumed**:
1. **Runtime precedence -- already correct, by construction, not by an explicit check.** `collectJobs` (now `collectJobsAndStale`) only ever builds a "needs enrichment" job for a field whose `DescriptionSource == DescriptionSourceNone`. A field that resolves to `DescriptionSourceModel` on a given run never reaches the checked-in lookup at all -- the gate itself, not a "prefer sourced" comparison, is what makes sourced win automatically. The founder's own hypothesis ("keys on 'has any description' rather than 'has a sourced description'") was NOT what the code did -- confirmed by direct reading, not assumed correct.
2. **Artifact hygiene -- genuinely broken, confirmed and fixed.** Nothing anywhere in the pipeline ever removed a checked-in entry once it became stale. `loadCheckedInDescriptions` reads the file; nothing ever wrote it back. A stale entry sat in the committed JSON forever, permanently unused (lookup only ever consults `DescriptionSourceNone` fields, which this one no longer is), silently implying an AI-inference happened for a field that's actually sourced now.

**The real fix**: `collectJobsAndStale` (renamed from `collectJobs`) now walks EVERY field, not just `DescriptionSourceNone` ones -- for any field resolving to `DescriptionSourceModel` that also has a checked-in entry, it's recorded as stale. `enrichDescriptions` prunes every stale entry from `opts.checkedIn` in place (a new `checkedInDescriptions.prune` method, dropping the resource's own entry entirely once it has no fields left, not leaving an empty `{}` block) and returns the real count. `cli/sdk.go`'s own `writeGeneratedSDK` persists the pruned map back to the real `sdk/providers/descriptions/<provider>.json` file whenever anything was actually pruned, printing a real, visible line (`sdk gen: <provider>: pruned N stale checked-in description(s)...`) -- a normal run with nothing stale never touches the file at all.

**Real, live proof against the ACTUAL already-committed data, not a synthetic fixture**: running `ubx sdk gen` against the real central config found 14 real, live stale entries -- 10 in `datadog.json`, 4 in `github.json`. Root cause confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed: every one of them was a checkpoint-6-era, hand-authored entry for a NESTED field (`datadog_api_key_response.api_key.name`, `github_deployment_protection_rule.app.id`, ...) -- exactly the class of field checkpoint 11's own later nested-attribute-description fix corrected, so these fields now correctly receive their real, wire-sourced description, and the checkpoint-6 text became stale the moment that later fix landed. This is a real, concrete confirmation that the bug this checkpoint fixes was not hypothetical -- it had already silently affected this exact arc's own committed artifact. Spot-checked the real generated code after pruning: `github_deployment_protection_rule`'s own `app.id` field now renders its real, sourced description with no `(AI-inferred)` suffix, not the old checkpoint-6 text.

**Verification discipline**: 3 new hermetic tests (`TestEnrichDescriptions_StaleCheckedInEntry_PrunedNotAppliedWhenSourced` -- both real halves in one test, sourced-wins AND stale-pruned, plus a still-genuinely-needed sibling entry proven to survive pruning untouched; `TestWriteCheckedInDescriptions_RoundTrips`; `TestCheckedInDescriptions_Prune_RemovesEmptyResourceEntry`). Whole `ubiquex` repo (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean. All six providers' generated Go trees `go build` clean after the real pruning run, individually confirmed.

## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 11 -- the real ceiling was a decode-time bug, not a documentation gap: nested-attribute descriptions were silently discarded before ever reaching the IR; real, live coverage nearly TRIPLED (9.8% -> 29.3%) fixing it, committed to main, 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own explicit go/no-go check before any further description-authoring or multi-source-merging work: real total field count, real per-provider quality samples. Delivered (see below), which surfaced a bigger, unplanned finding that the founder then explicitly asked to prioritize over the originally-scoped multi-source-merge task.

**The real finding, traced field by field, not inferred**: picked one real field (`kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.replicas`) and followed its own real description text through every real layer of the pipeline. Source spec (swagger.json): present. After Swagger2->OpenAPI3 conversion: present. After `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own `Translator.BuildTopLevel`: present. After `MergeResourceAttributes`: present. After the real tfplugin6 RPC round-trip, at the TOP level (`spec` itself): present. The moment you look at `spec`'s own children (`replicas`, `selector`, ...): gone. Root cause pinned exactly: `provider/schema.go`'s `nestedObjectCtyTypeFromV6` converts every attribute inside a real `NestedType` (protocol v6's own real nested-attribute mechanism, which `internal/schema/translate.go` deliberately builds for every real nested object in every dynamic provider) into a bare `cty.Type` -- and `cty.Type`, by design, carries VALUE SHAPE only, never carries Description/Required/Optional/Computed/Sensitive. This code is old (its own comment: written when the only known real-world NestedType user was one rare hashicorp/kubernetes resource, "zero AWS/Google attributes ever hit this") and simply predates the entire onboarding-pipeline arc's own later decision to make NestedType the DOMINANT shape for six real providers -- nobody had revisited whether this pre-existing, reasonable-at-the-time conversion was still safe.

**Aggregate scope of the loss, confirmed live before writing any fix**: the full source `swagger.json` is 98.6% described at the schema-property level (3,375 of 3,424). The pipeline's own generated Kubernetes output showed 3.1% sourced. That gap is almost entirely this bug, not a genuine documentation gap in Kubernetes' own real API -- and the severity pattern across providers (kubernetes 3.1%, azure 2.7% -- the two deepest-nesting real schemas -- lowest; flatter providers retained more) is exactly what this specific bug predicts, not six independent per-provider issues.

**The real fix, additive and narrowly scoped**: `provider.Attribute` gains a new field, `NestedAttributes []Attribute` -- the real, recursive, per-nested-attribute metadata (Description/Required/Optional/Computed/Sensitive) a flat `cty.Type` has no room for, populated by a new `nestedAttributesFromV6` (mirrors `nestedObjectCtyTypeFromV6`'s own real recursive structure exactly, alongside it, not replacing it -- `Type`'s existing flattened-cty.Type role is untouched, since `ctyvalue.go`'s own real config-value encoding and every other consumer still needs exactly that). `sdk/codegen/ir.typeRefFromCty` now threads a `meta map[string]provider.Attribute` parameter through its own existing recursion (list/set/map/object, at every depth), looking up each nested field's own real metadata by name instead of leaving every non-top-level `ir.Field` permanently zero-valued. Protocol v5 (no `NestedType` concept at all) and any v6 attribute that never used `NestedType` are both unaffected -- `meta` is simply nil, the identical real "no extra metadata available" case that already existed, unchanged.

**Real, live, end-to-end proof, not simulated -- the number that matters**:

| Provider | Before | After | Real gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| azure | 2.7% | **54.4%** | +1,107 fields |
| google | 28.5% | **52.3%** | +1,490 fields |
| kubernetes | 3.1% | **23.5%** | +3,151 fields |
| github | 15.8% | **24.3%** | +410 fields |
| datadog | 4.7% | **13.3%** | +455 fields |
| aws (SQS only, Smithy path, no NestedType involved) | 0.0% | 0.0% | +0 (expected, out of scope for this fix) |
| **Aggregate (33,967 real fields)** | **9.8%** | **29.3%** | **+6,613 fields, real, sourced, zero authoring cost** |

Re-ran the full `ubx sdk gen --lang go` against the ENTIRE real central config after the fix; all six providers generated successfully, exit 0. All six providers' generated Go trees `go build` clean against a real, local `ubx-sdk-go` runtime checkout (individually confirmed, not just one). Spot-checked the real rendered text directly in generated code: `kubernetes_apps_deployment`'s own `Replicas` field now carries `// Number of desired pods. This is a pointer to distinguish between explicit zero and not specified. Defaults to 1.` -- the exact real source text, two nesting levels deep, previously empty. 2 new hermetic regression tests: `TestBlockFromV6_NestedTypeAttribute_MetadataSurvives` (`provider` package, two levels deep, all five metadata fields) and `TestFromSchema_NestedAttributeMetadata_Survives` (`sdk/codegen/ir`, confirms the fix reaches all the way to a real `ir.Field`, including `DescriptionSource`). Whole `ubiquex` repo (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean -- this is a change to core, shared provider-decoding code used by every real provider (`[providers]` AND `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` alike), so the whole-repo run mattered more than usual here; zero regressions.
