## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 10 -- Go/Python computed-field label-visibility gap closed via a new, real Attrs type per resource, and a real, pre-existing IR bug it exposed (a leading-digit wire name) fixed at the source, committed to main, 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own priority 3, the last item on this session's own list: the Go/Python computed-field label-visibility gap checkpoint 6 found (TS already showed the AI-inferred label correctly for computed-only fields like `id`/`node_id`; Go/Python showed nothing at all, for ANY description, sourced or AI-inferred).

**Root cause, confirmed by direct inspection before writing any fix**: Go's `ResourceFile` builds exactly one struct per resource (`XxxConfig`), filtered through `fieldIsSettable` -- and `collectNestedStructs` (the function that registers a nested object's own struct declaration at all) was ALSO gated by the identical filter, at the TOP level. A computed-only top-level object field (e.g. `github_deployment_protection_rule`'s own `app`) therefore had its ENTIRE nested subtree skipped from collection, at ANY depth -- not just missing a comment, missing a declaration entirely. Python's `collectNestedDataclasses` had the identical shape. TS never had this problem: its own `XxxAttrs` interface already walks every field unconditionally (confirmed by reading ts.go directly, not assumed).

**The real fix**: both `sdk/codegen/templates/go` and `.../py` gain a new `XxxAttrs` struct/dataclass per resource -- mirrors TS's own `XxxAttrs` exactly, listing every real field (settable or computed-only) with its own real doc comment (sourced/AI-inferred/none, the identical `fieldDocComment` helper already used for Config). The nested-struct/dataclass collection loop (`collectNestedStructs`/`collectNestedDataclasses`) is now called unconditionally for every field, not just settable ones -- safe, because it's already a real, dedup-by-shape cache (`r.seenShapes`): an already-covered shape (referenced from Config) is a cache hit, a newly-covered one (a computed-only field's own nested object) gets a real declaration for the first time, shared by both Config and Attrs. **Real, deliberate, honestly-scoped limitation, named in the code and here, not silently implied complete**: Attrs is a real, declared type, but nothing in `ubx-sdk-go`/`ubx-sdk-python`'s own separate runtime repos currently constructs or returns a value of this shape -- confirmed by reading `ubx-sdk-go/runtime/runtime.go` directly: its own `*Computed` type is an opaque, string-addressed reference for cross-resource wiring (`.Field(name)` addressing), never a materialized Go value, and `FieldMap`/`ResourceBinding` are explicitly documented as Config-struct-specific (settable-field wire-name mapping), not a computed-value reader. Building a real runtime mechanism to materialize `Attrs` values is separate, substantial, cross-repo work, deliberately not attempted this checkpoint (would need real, separately-verified changes to two SEPARATE runtime repos, per CLAUDE.md's own rule 8 discipline) -- Attrs exists today purely so every field's own real description has a real, visible home, which is what "genuinely visible, not a footnote" actually asked for.

**A real, pre-existing bug in `sdk/codegen/ir`, found live, fixed at the real source -- not silently worked around in the template layer**: making every field's nested tree reachable for the first time immediately broke real Go generation for `github_commit_comment` (a real Go parse failure: `expected '}', found 1`). Root-caused by direct fetch of GitHub's own real, live, published `reaction-rollup` schema: it has BOTH `+1` and `-1` as real property names (👍/👎 reaction counts). `+1` was already correctly skipped (`isValidWireName` rejects `+`). `-1` was NOT: `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own `ToSnakeCase` (upstream, a separate repo) converts the leading `-` to `_`, producing the wire name `_1` -- every individual character in `_1` (`_` and `1`) is individually allowed, so `isValidWireName`'s own character-set-only check passed it through -- but `pascalCase`'s own leading-underscore strip then collapsed it to a bare `1`, an invalid Go/Python identifier. This bug was REAL and PRE-EXISTING (nothing to do with this checkpoint's own Attrs change), but had never been TRIGGERED before, because `reactions` (this field's own parent) is computed-only at the top level, and Go/Python's prior, settable-fields-only nested-struct collection had never visited it. Fixed at the real source: `isValidWireName` now also rejects a name whose first non-underscore character is a digit (the exact real condition that produces an invalid identifier once translated), not just an individually-disallowed character. A real, direct regression test (`TestFromSchema_LeadingDigitAfterUnderscoreStrip_Skipped`) proves both the rejection (`_1`) and a deliberate control case that must still pass (`_valid2`, a digit that isn't leading once the underscore strips).

**Real, live, end-to-end proof, not simulated**: re-ran the full `ubx sdk gen` against the ENTIRE real central config, both `--lang go` and `--lang py`, all six providers, both exit code 0 -- zero failures. Confirmed the AI-inferred label now renders correctly for the exact real, checkpoint-6-authored GitHub fields that previously showed nothing (`github_label.node_id`, confirmed present in both the generated Go and Python trees). The generated Go tree for ALL SIX providers `go build`s clean against a real, local `ubx-sdk-go` runtime checkout (not just one provider -- every one, individually confirmed). Every generated Python file across all six providers parses clean via a real `ast.parse` sweep (94-plus files across the largest providers). 4 new hermetic tests: `TestResourceFile_ComputedOnlyField_DescriptionVisibleInAttrs` and `TestResourceFile_ComputedOnlyNestedObject_GetsARealDeclaration` (Go), the identical field-visibility test (Python), plus the IR-layer regression test above. Whole `ubiquex` repo (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean.

**Verification discipline**: every fix in this checkpoint was confirmed against REAL, live data before being called done -- GitHub's own real, published OpenAPI spec (not a synthetic fixture) is what surfaced the `-1` bug in the first place; the fix was verified by re-running the exact same real pipeline, not just by the new unit test passing in isolation. Committed and pushed directly to `main` (this repo's own allowed convention), confirmed live via `gh api .../git/refs/heads/main`.

**Still honestly ahead**: a real, functional computed-attribute-READING mechanism for Go/Python's own Attrs type (cross-repo, substantial, not attempted); SigV4's own identical latent `credential_source=env` eager-validation gap (checkpoint 9, named, not fixed); the real volume of undescribed fields (checkpoint 9's own quantified split); Smithy's own real trait-based signal source; the real doc-corpus generation for any working provider (where Attrs' own new field list is also relevant); the full verification bar's remaining pieces; AWS's own "many schema entries, one combined target repo" reconciliation; real REST wire execution for GCP; repo-creation automation; `version-watch.yml` wiring. **All three of this session's own explicitly ordered priorities are now done.**

## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 9 -- Azure's real oauth2 eager-credential design bug fixed (a real design fix, not a workaround), ALL SIX central-config providers now generate successfully in one real run for the first time, real per-provider sourced-coverage split reported, pushed to ubx-provider-dynamic (not merged), 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own priority order: (1) fix Azure's eager oauth2 credential validation as a real design fix, not a workaround -- "schema fetching shouldn't require valid credentials at all"; (2) report the real sourced-description coverage split across all providers, the way GCP's 28% was measured; (3) the Go/Python computed-field label gap. This entry covers (1) and (2); (3) is this session's own next, separate work.

**(1) The real design bug, precisely**: `internal/auth/oauth2.go`'s own `buildOAuth2ClientCredentials` read `client_id_env`/`client_secret_env`'s real environment-variable VALUES eagerly, at `Build()` time -- called unconditionally by `main.go`'s own `run()` for EVERY declared `[dynamic_providers.<name>.auth]` table the instant this binary starts, including a real, honest schema-only launch (`GetProviderSchema`, never `Configure`) that needs no credential at all. `api_key_header` (github/datadog's own real config) never had this problem: its own `Apply` already re-reads its env var fresh on every real call, never validating presence until a real request is actually being signed. Root cause was a real, deliberate DESIGN choice (checkpoint-1-era comment, quoted honestly in the diff): "client ID/secret are resolved once here, at Build time... real OAuth2 client credentials don't rotate."  That reasoning conflated two genuinely separate real concerns -- WHEN a credential's presence is first checked (should be lazy, deferred to actual use) versus whether the resulting `TokenSource` caches/reuses a real, already-issued token across many calls (should stay eager-ONCE, for real efficiency) -- checkpoint 9 separates them.

**The real fix**: `oauth2ClientCredentialsAuth` now holds its own parsed params and resolves the real credential + builds the real `oauth2.TokenSource` exactly ONCE, lazily, inside `Apply` (`sync.Once`), not inside `Build`. `Build` itself still validates real config SHAPE eagerly (`token_url`/`client_id_env`/`client_secret_env` non-empty -- a real config mistake, legitimate to fail fast on, unchanged) but never touches `os.LookupEnv` or the real token endpoint until a real HTTP request actually needs signing. This is the identical real discipline `api_key_header` already had -- oauth2 now matches it, generalized, not Azure-specific: ANY real provider using `oauth2_client_credentials` benefits, not a special case carved out for Azure alone.

**A related, real, NOT-fixed latent gap, found while auditing for the same root-cause class, honestly named rather than silently expanded into**: `internal/auth/sigv4.go`'s own `buildSigV4` has the IDENTICAL eager-at-Build shape for `credential_source = "env"` (the DEFAULT) -- `resolveCredentialsProvider` calls `os.LookupEnv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"/"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY")` eagerly and fails Build outright if unset. NOT currently triggered by the real, central config's own `aws` entry (which deliberately uses `credential_source = "profile"`, whose own `awsconfig.LoadDefaultConfig` call does NOT eagerly require real credential values to be present -- it defers that to the credential provider's own real `Retrieve()` call, i.e. Apply time, already correct). Not fixed this checkpoint: fixing SigV4's `env` case properly needs a real, lazy `aws.CredentialsProvider` wrapper (the AWS SDK's own static-credentials constructor takes concrete strings, not deferred env lookups, unlike oauth2's simpler shape) -- a real, small, additional change, deliberately not bundled into this checkpoint's own explicit scope (the confirmed, live-blocking Azure bug), named here so it isn't silently forgotten.

**Real, live, end-to-end proof, not simulated -- the real milestone this fix unlocked**: ran the full `ubx sdk gen --lang go` against the ENTIRE real central config (`sdk/providers/.ubx/config`, all 6 declared providers) with `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`/`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` deliberately unset (confirmed unset first, not assumed). **Every one of the six providers generated successfully, real exit code 0, zero failures reported** -- the first time in this entire arc that a single `ubx sdk gen` run against the real central config has succeeded end-to-end for all six declared entries at once (checkpoint 3: 4 of 6; checkpoint 7: still blocked on this exact bug after the resourcemap fix). Azure specifically: 0 resources (every prior checkpoint) -> 19 resources, 2,138 fields -- the generated Go tree `go build`/`go vet` clean against a real, local `ubx-sdk-go` runtime checkout, the identical real verification bar every other provider in this arc uses. 2 new hermetic tests in `internal/auth/oauth2_test.go`: one proving `Build` never requires the named env vars to exist at all (the direct regression test for the bug itself), one proving the real token endpoint is still hit exactly ONCE across three real `Apply` calls (a real, direct check that deferring the TIMING of TokenSource construction did not regress the real, standard OAuth2 caching/reuse behavior the original eager design existed to provide -- the existing `TestOAuth2ClientCredentials_RealTokenExchange` alone couldn't distinguish "cached" from "re-exchanged every call" against a fixed-response fake endpoint).

**(2) The real per-provider sourced-description coverage split, captured live in the same run above -- the number the founder said "determines how much description authoring the full regeneration actually requires"**:

| Provider | Source | Fields | Sourced | AI-inferred | None |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| google (GCP Compute) | Discovery Docs | 6,235 | **1,774 (28%)** | 0% | 4,461 (72%) |
| github | OpenAPI | 4,832 | **764 (16%)** | 17 (0%) | 4,051 (84%) |
| datadog | OpenAPI | 5,272 | **247 (5%)** | 10 (0%) | 5,015 (95%) |
| kubernetes | OpenAPI (Swagger2) | 15,492 | **483 (3%)** | 0% | 15,009 (97%) |
| azure (Compute) | OpenAPI (Swagger2) | 2,138 | **57 (3%)** | 0% | 2,081 (97%) |
| aws (SQS only) | Smithy | 4 | **0 (0%)** | 4 (100%, this session's own authored batch) | 0 |

Real, honest reading: GCP's Discovery Documents carry BY FAR the richest real, sourced prose (28%, roughly double GitHub's own next-best 16%) -- a real, structural property of that schema source, not an artifact of this pipeline. OpenAPI-sourced providers cluster low (3-5% for datadog/kubernetes/azure); GitHub is the one real outlier among them (16%), likely because GitHub's own real, published OpenAPI spec is unusually description-complete compared to Datadog's/Azure's/Kubernetes'. **The real, load-bearing implication for the founder's own stated question**: a full regeneration across these five real providers (excluding the already-tiny, already-100%-covered aws/SQS sample) would leave roughly 94-97% of ~34,000 real fields genuinely undescribed on OpenAPI/Swagger2 sources, and 72% undescribed even on GCP's own richer Discovery Docs -- description authoring at real, full-provider scale is a substantial, multi-session undertaking under the checked-in-artifact workflow (checkpoint 6), not a small tail task; the founder's own "batched across sessions" framing was accurate, not an underestimate.

**Verification discipline**: whole `ubx-provider-dynamic` suite (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean; pushed to the existing checkpoint branch (`onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`, PR #5, still draft, still open, never self-merged), confirmed live via `gh api .../git/refs/heads/...`.

## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 8 -- GCP Discovery Documents, the real third schema-source format, schema-layer proven live against the actual configured Compute spec (95 resources, 6,235 fields, real Go build), pushed to ubx-provider-dynamic (not merged), 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own priority 3: "GCP's Discovery Docs as a third schema-source format, alongside OpenAPI and Smithy." Founder explicitly agreed, mid-checkpoint, to scope this to schema-layer proof only -- the identical real precedent this arc's own Kubernetes checkpoint 1 set (discover + translate first, prove it live; real REST wire execution against a real cloud endpoint is separate, later work, the same staging Smithy's own real Phase 1 -> Phase 4 already used) -- since real CRUD execution can never be live-verified against GCP under this project's own standing "never touch a real cloud provider for verification" rule (CLAUDE.md) regardless of how much code gets written.

**Real, live research before writing any code, per this arc's own standing discipline**: fetched Google Cloud Pub/Sub's own real, published discovery document live and inspected its actual shape before designing anything. Two real, load-bearing findings that shaped the whole design:
1. A Discovery Document's own real CRUD signal is EXPLICIT and MORE reliable than OpenAPI's: resources are a real, recursive `resources.<name>.resources/methods` tree, with real, unambiguous method KEYS ("get"/"create" or "insert"/"patch" or "update"/"delete") -- no response-schema-identity heuristic (`internal/resourcemap`'s own real, necessary complexity for OpenAPI's flatter, less structured paths) is needed at all for this source.
2. A Discovery Document's own `schemas` dialect is close enough to OpenAPI's schema object (type/properties/items/additionalProperties/enum/description/readOnly/$ref) that a real, new schema-source engine could convert it into an already-resolved `*openapi3.Schema` tree and hand it STRAIGHT to `internal/schema.Translator`'s existing, mature, heavily-tested `BuildTopLevel` -- real code reuse of the one genuinely hard, load-bearing layer (nested object/array/map/union field translation), not a second, parallel implementation of it. Also confirmed live, directly, before relying on it: Discovery Documents carry NO required-field signal at the schema/body level at all (grepped Pub/Sub's own real schemas, not assumed) -- only `readOnly`, the identical OpenAPI convention `Translator` already reads -- so every converted property naturally resolves to Optional or Computed through `Translator`'s own existing, unchanged `fieldPolicy` logic.

**New package, `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s `internal/discoverydoc`**: `Load` (fetch+parse a real Discovery Document JSON over HTTP), `Discover` (the real, explicit method-key walk described above, `sort`-ed for determinism, real "skip a read-only node with a Note" discipline matching `resourcemap`'s own), `Build` (per resource: `Translator.BuildTopLevel` on the real, resolved create-request and read-response schemas, `MergeResourceAttributes`/`MergeSignalMaps` -- the identical real merge machinery `internal/dynserver.Build`'s OpenAPI path already uses, reused unchanged). `config.SchemaSourceDiscoveryDoc = "discovery_docs"` added as a real, fourth IMPLEMENTED tier (not a placeholder) -- the exact string value the central config's own comment had already anticipated since checkpoint 3. `cmd/ubx-provider-dynamic/main.go` gained a new branch mirroring the Smithy/OpenAPI branches exactly, including `--dump-signals` support; the normal serve path reuses `dynserver.Server` UNCHANGED for `GetProviderSchema` (confirmed by direct inspection that RPC reads only `ResourceType.Schema`, nothing else) -- every other real RPC on that Server would need `Client`/`ObjectType`/`PathParamAttr` this checkpoint never populates, a real, honest, named gap for the future execution checkpoint, not exercised by today's real schema-fetch/`--dump-signals` usage.

**Two real bugs found live, both fixed before this checkpoint closed, neither found by inspection alone**:
1. A hand-built test fixture initially asserted the WRONG expected merge result for a readOnly field also referenced by the create request (Pub/Sub's own real `Topic` schema is shared verbatim between `create`'s request and the read response) -- `MergeResourceAttributes`'s own real, already-correct, already-documented rule ("both sides, create Optional: final Optional+Computed") was right; the test's own expectation was wrong. Fixed by correcting the assertion, not the code.
2. A REAL bug, caught only by actually generating Go code against the real, live, ALREADY-configured GCP Compute discovery document (`sdk/providers/.ubx/config`'s own long-standing `google` entry, 95 real resources -- Pub/Sub alone never exercised this): a Discovery Document's own resource-tree keys are camelCase (`backendBuckets`, `targetHttpProxies`), unlike OpenAPI's own already-snake_case ref names -- a raw camelCase noun reached the Go template's own real "only lowercase ascii + digits + underscore" wire-name guard and failed generation outright with `unsupported character 'B'`. Fixed by reusing `uschema.ToSnakeCase` (the identical, already-exported conversion `internal/schema/translate.go` already applies to every OpenAPI property name) on the resource noun before naming, with a new regression test.

**Real, live, end-to-end proof, not simulated, against the ACTUAL configured central-config entry, not just the smaller Pub/Sub research target**: `ubx sdk gen --lang go` against `https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis/compute/v1/rest` (real tfplugin6 RPC path, `provider.Launch`, not just `--dump-signals`) generated **95 real resource types, 6,235 fields, 28% real, sourced descriptions** (GCP's own Discovery Documents carry unusually rich real prose -- confirmed live, not assumed, the highest sourced-coverage percentage of any provider in this pipeline so far). The generated Go tree `go build`/`go vet` clean against a real, local `ubx-sdk-go` runtime checkout (the identical real sibling-repo-on-disk convention every other verification in this arc's own history uses). 6 new hermetic tests in `internal/discoverydoc/discoverydoc_test.go` (real Pub/Sub-shaped discovery, read-only-skip, readOnly-merge-semantics, self-referential-$ref cycle guard with a 2s timeout, array-of-objects resolution, the camelCase regression above). A known, pre-existing, ALREADY-documented naming-heuristic limitation carried over unchanged, not newly introduced: `resourcePolicies` -> `resource_policie` (the identical real "naive trailing-s-stripped, not a real inflection engine" limitation `resourcemap.deriveNoun`'s own fallback path already documents for OpenAPI).

**Central config comment updated** (`sdk/providers/.ubx/config`): the `[dynamic_providers.google]` entry's own header comment rewritten from "schema FORMAT genuinely not supported yet" to a real, honest account of what's now proven (schema layer, live-verified counts above) versus what's still deliberately out of scope (real REST wire execution).

**Verification discipline**: `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s whole suite (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean; pushed to the existing checkpoint branch (`onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`, PR #5, still draft, still open, never self-merged), confirmed live via `gh api .../git/refs/heads/...`. `ubiquex`'s own config-comment update committed and pushed directly to `main` (this repo's own allowed convention).

**Still honestly ahead**: real REST wire execution for GCP (Configure/Create/Read/Update/Delete actually calling `compute.googleapis.com` -- this checkpoint's own explicit, deliberate scope boundary); the oauth2_client_credentials eager-validation gap (checkpoint 7); the Go/Python computed-field label-visibility gap (checkpoint 6); the remaining real volume of undescribed fields across every provider; Smithy's own real trait-based signal source; the real doc-corpus generation for any working provider; the full verification bar's remaining pieces; AWS's own "many schema entries, one combined target repo" reconciliation; repo-creation automation; `version-watch.yml` wiring.

## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 7 -- Azure's real PUT-vs-POST resourcemap gap fixed and proven (0 -> 19 real resources), a new, separate, deeper Azure blocker found and honestly named, not fixed, pushed to ubx-provider-dynamic (not merged), 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own priority 2, described as "likely small and generic, ARM is not the only API that creates with PUT" -- confirmed correct on both counts.

**The real fix, in `ubx-provider-dynamic`** (`internal/resourcemap/resourcemap.go`, `findCreate`): widened the existing response-schema-identity create-matching loop from POST-only to POST-or-PUT. Confirmed live, via direct inspection of Azure's own real, published `Microsoft.Compute` spec, that this is the correct, minimal fix, not a heuristic guess: the real `virtualMachines/{vmName}` item path's GET, PUT, AND PATCH operations all reference the IDENTICAL `#/definitions/VirtualMachine` response schema -- the exact same response-schema-identity signal `findCreate` already used for POST works unchanged once PUT is a candidate method, with no separate same-item-path special case needed at all. The existing fewest-path-params tiebreak (already in place, for determinism) turns out to already correctly prefer a real POST-to-collection endpoint over an item-path PUT whenever a provider offers both for the same resource (an item path binds every one of its own path params, so it can never have fewer than its own creating collection endpoint) -- confirmed with a new regression test (`TestFindCreate_PrefersPOSTOverPUTWhenBothMatch`), not just assumed safe for GitHub/Kubernetes/Datadog's own existing POST-based resources.

**Real, live, quantified proof**: `ubx-provider-dynamic --dump-signals` against Azure's real, live spec (schema-only, bypasses the separate auth blocker below entirely) went from 0 resources (every checkpoint 1-6 run) to **19 real resources** -- `azure_virtual_machine`, `azure_virtual_machine_extension`, `azure_virtual_machine_scale_set`, `azure_availability_set`, `azure_capacity_reservation`, `azure_capacity_reservation_group`, `azure_dedicated_host`, `azure_dedicated_host_group`, `azure_image`, `azure_interconnect_block`, `azure_proximity_placement_group`, `azure_restore_point`, `azure_restore_point_collection`, `azure_ssh_public_key_resource`, and 5 more -- every one of them a real PUT-to-item-path ARM resource this package could not see at all before this fix. 2 new hermetic tests (`TestDiscover_ARMShapedCreateIsPUTOnTheSameItemPath`, the regression guard above); whole suite (`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`) clean. Pushed to the existing checkpoint branch (`onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`, PR #5, still draft, still open, never self-merged).

**A real, new, SEPARATE blocker found one layer deeper, honestly named, deliberately NOT fixed this checkpoint (out of today's explicit "resourcemap gap" scope)**: a full `ubx sdk gen` run against Azure still fails, but no longer at resourcemap -- it now fails at `auth.Build("oauth2_client_credentials", ...)`, which validates `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`/`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` are RESOLVABLE (present in the environment) eagerly, at build time, before ANY RPC is made -- even for a real schema-only launch (`GetProviderSchema`, never `Configure`) that needs no real credential at all. Confirmed this is a genuine asymmetry, not a universal rule: `api_key_header` auth (github/datadog's own real config) builds successfully with no credential present at all, deferring any real "missing env var" failure to actual request-signing time (which schema-only fetch never reaches) -- `oauth2_client_credentials` alone validates eagerly. This conflicts with the "no Configure, no real credentials needed" principle every schema-fetch code path in this pipeline already documents and relies on (`cli/dynamicprovider.go`'s own doc comments, this file's own prior checkpoints). Not fixed here: changing `internal/auth`'s own oauth2 builder to defer validation is a genuinely separate concern (auth-resolution timing, not resource discovery), potentially affects real `ship`/apply-time safety guarantees for OTHER real callers of `auth.Build` this session did not audit, and was not what today's explicit "PUT-vs-POST" task named. A real, honest, next gap for whoever picks this up -- Azure's schema CAN now be discovered and translated correctly (proven above via `--dump-signals`, which bypasses `auth.Build` entirely), but a normal `ubx sdk gen` run against it still can't complete without either a real Azure credential (never to be used for this pipeline's own verification, per this repo's own standing "never touch a real cloud provider for verification" rule) or a real fix to `internal/auth`'s own oauth2 builder.

**Still honestly ahead**: the oauth2_client_credentials eager-validation gap just found; GCP's own real Discovery Docs schema-source engine (this session's own next, immediate priority); Smithy's own real trait-based signal source; the Go/Python computed-field label-visibility gap (checkpoint 6); the remaining real volume of undescribed fields; the real doc-corpus generation for any working provider; the full verification bar's remaining pieces; AWS's own "many schema entries, one combined target repo" reconciliation; repo-creation automation; `version-watch.yml` wiring.

## Generic provider onboarding pipeline: CHECKPOINT 6 -- cost-driven redesign to a checked-in description artifact, real signal gap (constraints/enum) closed in ubx-provider-dynamic, real coverage numbers exist for the first time, committed to main, 2026-08-19

**Continuation, same no-ticket-ID arc.** Founder's own explicit, cost-driven redesign mid-arc: no live Claude API calls at generation time by default -- no budget for real per-field billing across four-plus providers at real volume. Descriptions become a real, checked-in, committed data file the pipeline reads at codegen time; `--describe` (the real, live API path, checkpoint 4/5) stays in the code as the "right long-term design once budget exists," explicitly not the default. **(1) The real signal gap, closed, in `ubx-provider-dynamic`** (branch `onboarding-pipeline-kubernetes-checkpoint`, PR #5, pushed, not merged): new `internal/schema/signals.go` -- `CollectSignals(s *openapi3.Schema) map[string]*FieldSignal`, a smaller, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE walk over the same `*openapi3.Schema` tree `translate.go`'s own mature, heavily-tested `Translator` walks, extracting `Enum`/`Minimum`/`Maximum`/`MinLength`/`MaxLength`/`Pattern` -- the real fields `tfprotov6.SchemaAttribute` has no wire slot for at all (checkpoint 5's own finding). **A real bug, found live, fixed before this checkpoint closed**: the first default value chosen for `--descriptions-dir`, `"sdk/providers/descriptions"`, silently assumed the process's own CWD is the repo root -- but this pipeline's own real, established convention (checkpoint 3) is to run `ubx sdk gen` FROM `sdk/providers/` (where the central config itself lives), so the relative default resolved to a nonexistent, doubled `sdk/providers/sdk/providers/descriptions` and produced a real, live run reporting 0 AI-inferred fields despite a real, committed descriptions file existing right there. **A real, structural finding from that same live run, honestly reported, not silently worked around**: the visible "AI-inferred" label renders correctly in ALL THREE languages for a SETTABLE field (`Required || Optional || !Computed`), but for a genuinely COMPUTED-ONLY field (no `Required`, no `Optional` -- the common shape for `id`/`node_id`/`created_at`/`updated_at`, exactly the kind of field this session's own real authoring batch mostly targeted), **Go and Python have no rendering location for ANY field's description at all**, sourced or AI-inferred -- confirmed live: `aws_sqs_queue.queue_url` (computed-only) got no comment in generated Go, while `attributes`/`queue_name`/`tags` (all settable) did; grepping the entire generated `github` Go and Python trees for "AI-inferred" after authoring 17 real, mostly computed-only field descriptions found ZERO matches in both languages, while the identical fields correctly showed the label in generated **TypeScript** (which already has a separate `Attrs` interface covering every field, computed included -- confirmed working as designed). Deliberately NOT changed here -- redesigning what fields Go/Python's generated bindings expose is a genuinely larger, separate change to the runtime/codegen contract, well beyond "render an existing description visibly," and out of this checkpoint's own explicit scope. Named, not silently worked around: a real, honest limitation for whoever authors descriptions next -- computed-only field descriptions are real (stored in `ir.Field`, counted in coverage, usable by a future doc-corpus generator that isn't bound by the SDK's own settable-field scope) but invisible in generated Go/Python code specifically until/unless that separate gap is addressed.

Both the `[providers]` loop and the `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` loop now thread a `*describe.Generator` through `generateOneProvider`/`generateOneDynamicProvider`/`writeGeneratedSDK` (all three signatures widened to return `(path string, resourceCount int, coverage descriptionCoverage, err error)`), collecting `perProviderCoverage`/`coverageOrder` and printing `formatCoverageReport(...)` at the end of RunE when `--describe` is set. The one real bug this pass caught before it ever ran live: the `[dynamic_providers.<name>]` loop's own call site was left on the OLD 3-return-value signature after `generateOneDynamicProvider`'s own signature had already been widened -- a real compile error, caught by `go build ./...` before any live run, not live.
4. **The visible "AI-inferred" label itself, in all three language templates** (`sdk/codegen/templates/{go,py,ts}`) -- a real, load-bearing finding: **none of the three templates rendered ANY field-level doc comment at all before this checkpoint**, sourced or otherwise (confirmed via a direct, deliberate grep for `.Description` across all three `*.go` template files -- zero matches). This means the "AI-inferred" label task was never just "add a suffix to an existing comment" -- it required building doc-comment rendering itself, for every field, in every language, for the first time, as this checkpoint's own real prerequisite. New `fieldDocComment(f ir.Field, pad string) string` in each of the three template packages (independently, matching each language's own real doc-comment convention -- `// ...` for Go, `# ...` for Python since a dataclass attribute has no real runtime-visible docstring form, `/** ... */` TSDoc for TS since that's what real editors surface as hover text): `DescriptionSourceModel` renders the description plain; `DescriptionSourceAIInferred` renders the identical description with a visible `" (AI-inferred)"` suffix; `DescriptionSourceNone` renders nothing at all -- no comment is more honest than a fabricated one. A shared `oneLineDescription` helper collapses real, source-carried internal newlines (confirmed live necessary against Kubernetes' own real CRD field prose in checkpoint 2-3) to spaces in each package; the TS variant additionally escapes a literal `"*/"` so a description can never prematurely terminate the TSDoc comment it's rendered inside -- the one real, language-specific injection risk this label introduces, not present in Go/Python's own single-line comment forms.

**Real conformance results, GitHub (`github_full_repository`)**:
- Probe 1 (identity-shape, live): **no finding**. `owner_path`+`repo` (see the real naming-collision finding below) is the type's own real, non-decomposable lookup key -- no smaller subset to compare against, the harness's own documented "nothing to compare" case, not a fabricated pass.

- Probe 4 (drift-detectability, live): **real, live-CONFIRMED finding** -- two consecutive, untouched reads of the same real repo returned genuinely different observed state. Root-caused directly (not guessed): the response's own real `temp_clone_token` field is a fresh, one-time-use value GitHub's own API mints on every single read, confirmed by two back-to-back `gh api` calls returning two different real token strings with zero mutation in between. This is the real `hashicorp/time` class docs/conformance-harness.md already names as a legitimate type characteristic, not a ubx-provider-dynamic bug -- the correct real mitigation is a `drift.ignore = ["temp_clone_token"]` entry in a stack's own `.ubx/config` (Phase 3's own existing mechanism), not a code change.

Full account: `839333509514`, region `us-east-1`, real queue created and destroyed, nothing left behind.

**Datadog**: **not run this session** -- no `DATADOG_API_KEY`/`DATADOG_APP_KEY` in this environment, confirmed directly (not assumed) before asking the founder, who chose to skip rather than substitute. A real, honest gap, not a pass or a fail -- Datadog's own real conformance status remains unknown until a future session runs this with real credentials.

**Two real, genuine bugs found and fixed in `ubx-provider-dynamic` itself** (separate PR there, `pull/4`), neither visible from schema inspection alone, both found only because this phase actually tried a real, live `ReadResource` rather than trusting a clean schema build:
1. **Path-parameter/response-attribute name collision**: GitHub's own real read path is `/repos/{owner}/{repo}`, but the response body ALSO carries its own real `owner` object field (login/id/avatar_url/...). `ensurePathParamsPresent` silently trusted the existing, wrong-typed attribute -- broke every real `ReadResource`/`ApplyResourceChange` call for the type outright with `extractStringAttrs`' own real "cannot be used as a path parameter" error. Fixed: on a genuine type collision, synthesize a distinctly-named path-only attribute instead (`owner` -> `owner_path`) and thread the real template-param-name -> attribute-name mapping (new `ResourceType.PathParamAttr`/`CreatePathParamAttr`) through every real call site that previously assumed the two names were always identical (`extractStringAttrs`, `requestBody`'s own exclude list, `carryForwardFields`).
2. **A real, hard `terraform-plugin-go` library constraint**: `tftypes.Object`'s own `OptionalAttributes` field, set on every real nested object value (`objectValueType` -- objects inside a List/Map element, or a merged `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` branch), panics UNCONDITIONALLY the instant `Object.UsableAs` is called with it non-empty -- confirmed directly against that library's own real source (`tftypes/object.go`: "Objects with OptionalAttributes cannot be used."), not assumed from behavior alone. A real, permanent constraint, not a version-specific bug: `OptionalAttributes` is only ever safe for a resource's own top-level `Block` object, never a nested value object, since every real state value (every `ReadResource`/`ApplyResourceChange` response) flows through msgpack, which hits this exact panic path. Fixed: never set it in `objectValueType`.

Both fixes confirmed live: `github_full_repository`'s own `ReadResource` failed with two DIFFERENT real errors before these fixes (first the path-param type mismatch, then, once that was fixed, the `OptionalAttributes` panic underneath it), and succeeded cleanly (a real 7241-byte decoded response) after both.

**Verification discipline**: `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean in both repos (hermetic), `UBX_LIVE_VALIDATION=1 go test ./...` clean in `ubx-provider-dynamic` (GitHub, Datadog schema-only, AWS Smithy). `ubiquex`'s own changes (`provider/client.go`, `conformance/*.go`) committed and pushed directly to `main` (this repo's own allowed convention), confirmed live via `gh api .../git/refs/heads/main`. `ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own fix commit is PR `github.com/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic/pull/4`, confirmed live via `gh api .../pulls/4` (`state: open`, `mergeable_state: clean`) -- not merged, per that repo's own PR-only discipline.

**This closes UBI-158's full five-phase arc.** Real, load-bearing conclusion per the ticket's own stated reasoning: trust for this Dynamic Provider is now backed by the same real, falsifiable probe suite every hand-written HashiCorp provider is held to -- two real bugs it actually caught and fixed, one real structural type-classification finding honestly documented (not hidden), one real environment gap honestly reported as unresolved (not faked as a pass), and one real provider (Datadog) honestly reported as not yet run rather than assumed clean.

**Real protocol distribution across all 430 real AWS Smithy service models -- direct file sampling, not

(`restXml: 0`, `ec2Query: 0` -- known-wrong results, since Checkpoint 1's own research had already
directly confirmed S3 uses restXml and EC2 uses ec2Query; diagnosed as GitHub code search excluding
large files, S3's model is ~3MB, EC2's is ~6.6MB, from its index). Replaced with a real, direct
range-fetch-then-grep sweep of all 430 real service model files (full file list obtained via one real
GitHub Git Trees API call, `recursive=1`, rather than 430 separate directory-listing calls). Real,
confirmed result: `restJson1` 256 (59.5%), `awsJson1_1` 102 (23.7%), `awsJson1_0` 50 (11.6%), `awsQuery`
15 (3.5%), `restXml` 4 (0.9%, but includes S3), `ec2Query` **1** (0.2%, EC2 only -- confirmed genuinely
exclusive, not a sampling gap). One real service (`partnercentral-revenue-measurement`) declares no
`aws.protocols#*` trait at all on its own service shape -- a real data-quality gap, not a scan bug
(confirmed by direct inspection). `cloudwatch` declares two protocols (`awsJson1_0` +
`awsQueryCompatible`) -- Checkpoint 1's own existing `resolveProtocol` first-match preference order
already handles this correctly, unchanged.

**Real, load-bearing finding that reshaped the whole wire-execution design**: the JSON body/response a
real AWS request/response uses is always keyed by the Smithy shape's own real member name (`QueueUrl`),
never the schema's translated snake_case attribute name (`queue_url`). `internal/smithy/wireexec`
re-derives this mapping at request/response time directly from the model via the same
`uschema.ToSnakeCase` the translator itself used to build the schema -- one real source of truth,
consulted twice, rather than threading a parallel name map through `BuiltResource`.

**Real, deliberate deviation from an implicit assumption in the original ticket, confirmed not
guessed**: AWS's own published Smithy models carry **no field at all** for `awsJson1_0`/`awsJson1_1`'s
own real `X-Amz-Target` header prefix. Confirmed by diffing real `aws-cli --debug` request traces
against the real, same-session-fetched model files for three structurally different services: SQS's
real prefix is `AmazonSQS` (an `"Amazon"+sdkId` shape), DynamoDB's is `DynamoDB_20120810` (service name
+ real API version, a genuinely DIFFERENT shape), and grepping both real model files directly for either
string confirms neither appears anywhere in the model at all. A blanket `"Amazon"+sdkId` heuristic would
have silently misfired against DynamoDB-shaped services with AWS's own real `UnknownOperationException`.
`target_prefix` is therefore required, explicit `.ubx/config` for any Smithy-sourced provider whose
protocol resolves to `awsJson1_0`/`awsJson1_1` (`config.Provider.TargetPrefix`), never guessed.

**Real wire protocol implementation** (`internal/smithy/wireexec`): all six real protocols dispatched on
the model's own declared trait -- `restJson1`/`restXml` share one real REST-binding codec (`httpLabel`
path substitution, including Smithy's own real "greedy label" `{Key+}` syntax confirmed live against
S3's `GetObject`; `httpQuery`; `httpHeader`), `awsJson1_0`/`awsJson1_1` share one real JSON-RPC codec
(flat body, `X-Amz-Target` header), `awsQuery`/`ec2Query` share one real form-encoded codec
(`Action`/`Version` + flattened members, real `<OperationName>Result` XML-response unwrapping, confirmed
live against a real SNS `ListTopics` response shape via `aws-cli --debug`). `restexec.Client` gained
`DoWithCodec` (`internal/restexec/codec.go`, purely additive -- `Do`/`doOnce` untouched, zero risk to
Phase 1-3's own tested REST-JSON path) so every real protocol reuses the identical real retry/backoff/
auth logic rather than reimplementing it four times. Real, documented, flagged gap (not silently
worked around): `restXml` REQUEST bodies (schema-guided XML encoding) are not yet implemented -- rare (4
real services) and not needed by any of this checkpoint's own real verification targets; a restXml
operation with body members refuses loudly rather than silently dropping fields.

**Real SigV4 signing** (`internal/auth/sigv4.go`, replacing Phase 2's stub): `aws-sdk-go-v2/aws/signer/v4`,
all three real credential sources (`env`/`profile`/`instance_role`) via `aws-sdk-go-v2/config`'s own
real, standard credential chain, wrapped in `aws.CredentialsCache` for real automatic refresh. **Real,
confirmed finding: the `Authenticator` interface (`Apply(req *http.Request) error`) needed NO change at

## UBI-158 Phase 4 Checkpoint 1 (Dynamic Provider AWS via Smithy: schema + naming): CHECKPOINT, not closed -- real Smithy schema source, resource mapping, and naming-parity layer, proven against five real AWS models, PR opened not merged, 2026-08-19

**Own-call checkpoint split, per this session's own explicit invitation ("your call once you see the real
scope")**: Phase 4's own four pieces (Smithy schema source, SigV4 auth, wire protocols, naming
compatibility) split into two checkpoints -- **Checkpoint 1 (this entry)**: Smithy schema source +
resource mapping + naming parity, provable via discovery alone. **Checkpoint 2 (next)**: real
per-protocol wire execution (restJson1/restXml/awsJson1_x/awsQuery/ec2Query) + real SigV4 signing,
which genuinely need each other (SigV4 needs at least one real wire executor to sign real requests
against). Branch `ubi-158-phase-4-cp1-smithy-naming`, PR
`github.com/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic/pull/2`, confirmed live via `gh api .../pulls/2` (`state:
open`, `mergeable_state: clean`, 24 files changed) -- not merged, per this repo's own PR-only
discipline (Phase 3 onward).

**Fetched fresh from real, current `main` before starting, confirmed not assumed**: `git fetch` +
`git pull` showed Phase 3's own PR (`#1`) already merged by the founder (`gh api .../pulls/1`:
`merged: true`) -- local `main` fast-forwarded to the real remote HEAD (`364f38f`) before any Phase 4
work began, matching this session's own explicit instruction.

**Real, current Smithy source, confirmed directly, not assumed**: `github.com/aws/api-models-aws`
("API Models for all public AWS Services," real, public, AWS-owned), one JSON file per service at
`models/<service>/service/<api-version>/<service>-<api-version>.json`. Real, confirmed format: Smithy
2.0 JSON AST -- a flat `shapeId -> shape` map, no `$ref` resolution needed at all (unlike OpenAPI),
confirmed against five real, structurally different services read directly this session (SQS, S3,
DynamoDB, EC2, Lambda, plus SNS added later for a clean fifth parity example after Lambda's own real
data turned out incomplete -- see below).

**Real, load-bearing reuse, not a parallel translator, per this session's own explicit instruction**:
`ubx-provider-dynamic`'s own `internal/smithy` package converts Smithy shapes into the *identical*
`openapi3.Schema` tree Phase 1's `schema.Translator` already consumes, completely unchanged --
confirmed by literally calling `Translator.BuildTopLevel` on the adapter's own output in a real test
and getting correctly-translated tfplugin attributes back. Two real reuse wins, not merely claimed:
Smithy's own tagged-union (`union`) shape maps directly onto OpenAPI's `oneOf`, activating Phase 1's
existing lossy-collapse-to-union-of-properties path with zero new logic; a self-referential Smithy
shape (real, confirmed to exist in real AWS models -- recursive filter/expression trees) is caught by
Phase 1's existing cycle guard for free, because the adapter memoizes each shape's own conversion by
shapeId (the SAME `*openapi3.Schema` pointer on every reference), and that guard was already built
pointer-identity-generic, not OpenAPI-specific. `internal/schema`'s own `tfName` was exported as
`ToSnakeCase` for this reuse (both OpenAPI property names and Smithy operation nouns converge on the
identical ubx snake_case convention).

**Real format difference reconciled once, not left for the translator to know**: Smithy puts
`smithy.api#required` as a trait on each MEMBER, not a parent-level `required: [...]` list the way
OpenAPI/JSON-Schema does -- the adapter collects it into the parent's own `Required` list during
conversion, so by the time a Smithy-sourced schema reaches `schema.Translator` it looks exactly like
an OpenAPI one, no second convention needed downstream. Smithy's own `input`/`output` operation split
maps even more directly onto Phase 1's create-request/read-response merge pattern than OpenAPI's own
per-status-code responses did.

**Resource mapping is a genuinely new heuristic, not reused from Phase 1's OpenAPI resourcemap**: real,
confirmed finding -- none of the five real AWS Smithy models read this session declare Smithy `resource`
shapes in practice, despite the Smithy spec itself defining a real `resource` shape kind with CRUD
bindings. What every real service DOES use is a verb+noun operation-naming convention
(`CreateQueue`/`GetQueueAttributes`/`SetQueueAttributes`/`DeleteQueue`) -- `internal/smithy/resourcemap.go`
groups on that instead, with two real, documented heuristic refinements found live, not designed in
advance: (1) AWS's own real `Get<Noun>Attributes`/`Set<Noun>Attributes` convention (the read/update
operation is very often NOT bare `Get<Noun>`) needed a real preference-ordered match (exact ->
`Attributes`-suffixed -> shortest-prefix -> alphabetical, deterministic); (2) EC2's own real
`RunInstances` (not `CreateInstance`) needed `Run` added to the real create-verb vocabulary (a genuine,
cross-service AWS "launch" convention, not an EC2-only special case) plus a singular-preferred-over-
plural noun resolution, since the batch-shaped verb leaves a plural remainder ("Instances") but
HashiCorp's own real resource name is always singular (`aws_instance`).

**Naming compatibility layer -- the real, highest-risk piece, proven against real ground truth, not
assumed**: dumped `hashicorp/aws`'s own real, live, complete resource type name list (**1682 real
names**) via ubx's own real `provider.Acquire`/`provider.Launch` machinery against a real, running
`hashicorp/aws` 6.54.0 binary's own `GetProviderSchema` call -- the identical "schema-fetch, safe, no
credentials" mechanism this repo's own `docs/executor.md`/STATE.md history already established
(`cmd/schemadump` precedent), via a throwaway tool in `cmd/awsnames`, deleted before committing, same
discipline as that precedent. Embedded a snapshot of this real list directly into `ubx-provider-dynamic`
(`internal/smithy/data/`, `go:embed`) so naming resolution works with no network access.

**Real, aggregate parity result across five real services (107 resources discovered)**: 39 exact
formula matches (`aws_<endpointPrefix>_<noun>` -- SQS/S3/DynamoDB/SNS's own primary resources all
matched this way: `aws_sqs_queue`, `aws_s3_bucket`, `aws_dynamodb_table`, `aws_sns_topic`), 26
bare-fallback matches (`aws_<noun>`, no service infix -- confirmed live: `aws_instance`, `aws_vpc`,
`aws_subnet`, `aws_security_group` all drop EC2's own `ec2_` prefix entirely), **42 genuinely
unresolved** -- overwhelmingly EC2, and NOT a heuristic bug: HashiCorp's own real naming here tracks
AWS's own human, conceptual service boundaries (EC2 core compute, EBS storage, VPC networking) rather
than the literal Smithy/API service boundary -- confirmed live that `aws_ebs_volume`/`aws_ebs_snapshot`
use a real, DIFFERENT prefix (`ebs`, not `ec2`) for operations living in the exact same Smithy model,
while dozens of other real EC2-API resources (`aws_ec2_transit_gateway`, `aws_ec2_fleet`, ...) DO carry
the expected `ec2_` prefix. No algorithm operating on the Smithy model alone can derive this distinction,
since the model itself never encodes it -- a real, permanent limitation, honestly reported via
`StrategyUnresolved` rather than guessed at or silently forced to match.

**A real, separate data-quality finding, not a bug in this package**: AWS's own published Smithy model
for Lambda (`models/lambda/service/2015-03-31/lambda-2015-03-31.json`, confirmed there is only one file
at this path) binds only **13 of 85** real operation shapes to its own service shape
(`com.amazonaws.lambda#AWSGirApiService`) -- `CreateFunction`/`GetFunction` both exist as real, fully-
defined shapes in the file but are simply never referenced by the service's own `operations` list, the
one real, correct way Smithy defines a service's actual API surface. `Discover` therefore correctly,
honestly reports zero resources for this specific real data source rather than guessing by scanning
orphaned shapes (a real risk: pulling in operations that were deliberately, or accidentally, left
unbound). SNS substituted as Checkpoint 1's fifth real parity example instead, confirmed complete (42
bound operations, real `CreateTopic`/`GetTopicAttributes`/`SetTopicAttributes`/`DeleteTopic`).

**Real, deliberate deviation from UBI-158's own original three-tier schema_source design (openapi/
inline/aws_ccapi), flagged rather than silently folded in**: this session's own Phase 4 prompt named
"Smithy" as AWS's real schema source, not "aws_ccapi" (the original ticket's own CloudFormation Cloud
Control API registry tier) -- these are two real, genuinely different AWS schema sources (Smithy models
AWS generates its own SDKs from vs. the separate CloudFormation resource-provider schema registry), so
`SchemaSourceSmithy` is a real, new fourth `schema_source` value; `SchemaSourceAWSCCAPI` is left exactly
as it was, a real, distinct, still-unimplemented tier of its own.

**Honest about what Checkpoint 1 does NOT do**: `cmd/ubx-provider-dynamic/main.go` runs the full real

## UBI-158 Phase 3 (Dynamic Provider execution semantics): CHECKPOINT, not closed -- retry/backoff, per-operation timeouts, async polling, field-level drift, PR opened (not merged) as of this session's own explicit PR-workflow switch, 2026-08-18

**Real workflow switch, per this session's own explicit instruction**: from this phase onward,
`ubx-provider-dynamic` no longer takes direct pushes to `main` -- this session branched
(`ubi-158-phase-3-execution-semantics`), committed (`dd6d8ea`), pushed, and opened a real PR
(`github.com/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic/pull/1`, confirmed live via `gh api
repos/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic/pulls/1` -- `state: open`, `mergeable_state: clean`, 20 files
changed -- not just the `gh pr create` exit status). **Never self-merged, per this project's own
standing constraint** -- the PR is left open for review.

**Real, load-bearing correctness fix, found by reading ubx core's own source rather than assumed**:
this session's own explicit instruction was to "plug into ubx's own existing reconcile-by-query
executor behavior... rather than designing a parallel mechanism" -- reading `docs/executor.md` and
`core/executor/ship.go` (this repo) directly surfaced that every Phase 1/2 call site in
`ubx-provider-dynamic` was wrapping every REST failure -- including merely transient ones (a 503, a
dropped connection) -- as a terminal tfplugin `Diagnostic`, unconditionally. Confirmed against the
real classification boundary `cli/stateadapter.go`/`provider/provider.go` (this repo) implement: a
`Diagnostic`-bearing response (`err == nil` from the RPC call itself) becomes a
`*provider.DiagnosticError`, permanently terminal within one `ubx ship` invocation; a raw, propagated
RPC-level error (`err != nil` from the call itself) is treated as retryable/ambiguous, driving
`unknown_post_timeout` and reconcile-by-query. Fixed in `ubx-provider-dynamic`: `restexec.IsTerminal`
classifies a real, structured 4xx rejection (400/401/403/404/405/406/409/410/411/412/413/414/415/422/
451) as terminal; 408/429/5xx (already targeted by `restexec`'s own internal retry loop) and every
network-level/decode failure default to ambiguous -- the identical "fail open toward uncertain"
asymmetry this repo's own `docs/executor.md` UBI-44 finding already established for a real "lying
destroy." `dynserver`'s own `classifyRESTError` is the one real seam every CRUD RPC method now routes
through, returning `(nil, err)` (a plain Go error) for the ambiguous case rather than ever wrapping it
in a Diagnostic.

**A real, deliberate non-reimplementation, confirmed rather than assumed**: `ubx-provider-dynamic`
does NOT reimplement `reconcileLoop`/`reconcileDestroyLoop`/`eventualConsistencyBackoffSchedule` --
those are core-side mechanisms operating on tfplugin-level primitives (`ReadResource`/`Diagnostic`)
the provider sits on the other side of. A clean destroy response from `ubx-provider-dynamic` already
transparently triggers core's own universal post-destroy read-back (UBI-44) with zero extra code on
the provider's own side -- confirmed by re-reading `shipDestroyNode`'s own real logic (this repo)
rather than assumed. What Phase 3 mirrors instead is the same DISCIPLINE, one layer down, in REST
terms: a real backoff schedule for the provider's own upstream HTTP calls (driven by real
`Retry-After`/rate-limit signals, not ubx core's own AWS-tuned schedule), a real per-operation timeout
(confirmed core sets none of its own -- `cli/ship.go`'s `--timeout` is one shared budget for an entire
`ubx ship` run, not per-RPC), and mapping every outcome onto exactly the two signals core actually
understands (Diagnostic vs. plain error) -- never a third, ubx-core-shaped concept.

**Real transport-level retry/backoff** (`internal/restexec`, new `retry.go`/`classify.go`): `Retry-After`
(RFC 9110 §10.2.3, both delay-seconds and HTTP-date forms) and a configurable rate-limit-reset header
(`X-RateLimit-Reset`, confirmed live against a real `api.github.com` response this session, present on
every GitHub response but confirmed ABSENT on Datadog's own real `/api/v1/validate` 403 -- real APIs
genuinely differ, hence a config field, not a hardcoded header name) both win outright over the
exponential-with-jitter fallback, deliberately NOT clamped to `MaxBackoff` (a real server-told wait is
never a "guess" `MaxBackoff` should bound) -- a real bug caught and fixed by the test itself
(`TestDo_RespectsRealRetryAfterHeader` first failed against the original, wrongly-clamping
implementation). A second real, non-obvious finding recorded in the same test file: a
unix-timestamp-second-granularity reset header ("N seconds from now") truncates sub-second precision,
so a naive "assert ~N seconds elapsed" test is genuinely flaky, not a production bug -- fixed by
asserting a lower bound against a 2-second target instead.

**Per-operation timeouts** (`internal/dynserver/policy.go`, `server.go`'s own
`withOperationTimeout`): `[dynamic_providers.<name>.timeouts]`, one real budget per CRUD operation
kind, wrapped around each individual `restexec.Client.Do` call -- independent of and additional to
ubx core's own ambient `--ship` deadline, exactly the granularity this session's own research
confirmed core structurally cannot supply on its own.

**Generic async/long-running-operation polling** (`internal/dynserver/async.go`), deliberately not
AWS-shaped per this session's own explicit instruction: `[dynamic_providers.<name>.resources.<type>.async]`
names where to find a newly-started operation's own id (a real response header, e.g. `Location`, or a
body dot-path -- a header wins when both are configured, a stronger signal than a guessed body path),
where to poll it, which dot-path carries status, and which real status values are terminal
success/failure. On success, performs one more real read against the resource's own canonical URL for
final attributes (a job-status response is rarely the full resource representation) -- reusing
`readFromAPI`, not a second read mechanism. Outcomes map onto the identical two signals: a configured
failure status becomes a Diagnostic (real, certain); a poll-timeout with no terminal status becomes a
plain, propagated error (ambiguous, lets core's own reconcile-by-query take over on the next
`ReadResource`). Verified end to end against a real local HTTP server modeling a genuine 202+job-id/
poll/final-read flow (`TestApplyResourceChange_Create_AsyncPollsUntilSuccessThenReads` and two sibling
tests for the failure-status and poll-timeout paths) -- caught and fixed one real test-data bug along
the way (the async operation id's own field name collided with the resource schema's own "id"
attribute, a string-vs-integer type mismatch, not a production bug).

**Field-level drift rules** (`internal/dynserver/policy.go`): `ignore` reuses the exact same
carry-forward mechanism Phase 1's own path-param handling already established (`carryForwardFields`,
renamed from `allPathParams`) -- an ignored field's fresh API value is simply never written into
state, the identical mechanism, a second real reason to use it. `normalize` (a real, small, fixed
registry -- `lowercase`/`uppercase`/`trim`, never an arbitrary expression language) is applied
unconditionally to every fresh API response before it's ever recorded, so every recorded value is
already canonical from the moment it's first written -- no separate "normalize before comparing" step
needed anywhere else.

**Live re-verification, not just hermetic tests**: GitHub's and Datadog's real specs still discover
the identical 61/25 resource sets after this refactor (byte-identical resource-type lists and Note
counts to Phase 1/2's own runs). GitHub's real rate-limit headers (`X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/
Reset/Used/Resource`) parse correctly against a real live response. OAuth2 client-credentials flow
re-verified against a real, local RFC 6749-compliant token endpoint (still no genuine third-party
no-registration test server available, same real constraint Phase 2 already recorded).

**Full repo `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean** (45 real tests, live ones gated behind
`UBX_LIVE_VALIDATION=1`). No em dashes.

**Explicitly not done this phase**: SigV4 signing itself (Phase 4, per UBI-158's own original
5-phase structure), Smithy, the conformance gate.

## UBI-158 Phase 1 (Dynamic Provider generic engine): CHECKPOINT, not closed -- tfplugin v6 server, OpenAPI->tfplugin schema translation, resource mapping, config layer built and validated live against GitHub's and Datadog's real specs, in a NEW separate repo, 2026-08-18

**New repo, not this monorepo, per this session's own explicit instruction**: `~/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic`
(local only -- no remote created or pushed to this session; git-initialized, one commit, `1840ec3`).
Binary/config decisions this session's own prompt already settled (post-dating UBI-158's own Linear

**Real, deliberate deviation from this session's own prompt, flagged rather than silently
reconciled**: the prompt's own text says to read a `[providers.<name>]` block from `.ubx/config`.
Confirmed directly against `cli/config.go` (this repo): `.ubx/config` already has a real,

the standard `ConfigureProvider` RPC, never read from disk by the provider itself. Neither can
supply what Phase 1 actually needs: `GetProviderSchema` is called before `ConfigureProvider` ever
runs (confirmed: `provider/provider.go`'s `v6Provider.Schema` takes zero arguments), so a Dynamic-
Provider-backed resource's schema -- which depends on which real OpenAPI spec this instance
represents -- must already be known at process startup, not delivered after Configure. Resolved by
having the binary read its own, separate, non-colliding table directly off disk at startup instead:
`[dynamic_providers.<name>]` (`schema_source`, `schema_url`, `base_url`, plus a stubbed `[auth]`
sub-table per Phase 1's own explicit non-scope). Full reasoning recorded in
`ubx-provider-dynamic/internal/config/config.go`'s own doc comment.

**Protocol version, confirmed against real ubx source, not assumed**: `provider/handshake.go` shows
ubx's own client advertises both v5 and v6 (`supportedAppProtocolVersions = []int{5, 6}`) and picks
whichever a launched binary negotiates -- v6 is the modern protocol, real HashiCorp binaries built on
`terraform-plugin-framework` (not legacy SDKv2) already speak it, and this session's prompt directed
building against v6, so `ubx-provider-dynamic` speaks v6 only (no legacy-v5 fallback needed for a
brand-new binary). Implemented via `terraform-plugin-go`'s own real, official `tfprotov6`/`tf6server`
package (v0.31.0, the identical module `provider/tfplugin6/tfplugin6.pb.go`'s own header cites as its
source) rather than hand-rolling the gRPC handshake/serve loop -- confirmed its magic cookie
key/value (`TF_PLUGIN_MAGIC_COOKIE` / `d602bf8f...`) match `provider/handshake.go`'s own real
constants exactly, so a `ubx-provider-dynamic` process is a genuine drop-in for `provider.Launch`,
zero special-casing.

**Layer 2 (schema translation) -- the real, load-bearing findings, the ticket's own "most important"
ask**: uses protocol v6's real nested-ATTRIBUTES feature (`SchemaAttribute.NestedType`/`SchemaObject`,
not the legacy block-nesting mechanism) -- the correct, exact fit for OpenAPI's own
properties-of-an-object shape. `oneOf`/`anyOf` is the single genuinely lossy case, three real,
distinct outcomes depending on the branches' own shapes (all documented via `Note`s attached to the
exact field path, never silently flattened): all-same-primitive branches collapse to that primitive
(not lossy in any way that matters -- only per-branch format/enum metadata is lost); all-object
branches collapse to the UNION of every branch's own properties, all Optional (real, documented loss:
mutual exclusivity and each branch's own required fields aren't enforced); structurally incompatible
mixed branches (primitive+object+array together) become `tftypes.DynamicPseudoType`, a real, native
protocol feature -- not a workaround -- for "the shape isn't known until a value actually arrives."
`allOf` is NOT lossy (real property union, JSON Schema's own composition semantics, not a compromise).
Optionality is derived per-schema from OpenAPI's real, distinct signals (`required` list, `readOnly`,
`writeOnly` -- the last maps onto protocol v6's own real, native `WriteOnly` flag, a clean, exact fit,
no loss at all); the Optional+Computed ("provider may default this") combination a real resource needs
is a separate, resource-level merge (`schema.MergeResourceAttributes`) combining a create-request
schema's own translation with a read-response schema's own translation by field name, since a single
schema alone has no basis to know that combination on its own.

**A real, serious bug found and fixed during live validation, not by inspection**: the translator had
no cycle detection. Live validation against Datadog's own real, published spec (not GitHub's) hung
with unbounded recursion -- confirmed directly (not assumed) via a stuck test process showing 6GB+ RSS
and climbing, diagnosed by `kill -QUIT` for a goroutine dump after ruling out network blocking (idle
CPU, no open sockets) as the cause. Root cause: a genuinely self-referential OpertAPI schema (Datadog's
own logs-pipeline `processors` field nests processors within processors; likely also present in
`widgets`/dashboard content). Fixed with a real cycle guard (`Translator.active`, a stack of
`*openapi3.Schema` pointers currently being expanded -- kin-openapi memoizes every `$ref` resolution to
one stable pointer per component, making pointer identity a reliable, cheap test) plus a depth cap as
defense-in-depth; a detected cycle degrades that one field to `DynamicPseudoType` with a `Note`, same
honest-degradation discipline as the `oneOf`/`anyOf` cases. A dedicated test
(`TestBuildAttribute_SelfReferentialSchema_DoesNotHang`, goroutine + 5s timeout, not just "runs fast in
practice") reproduces this exact shape so it can't regress silently.

**Layer 3 (resource mapping) -- real finding, not assumed**: real REST APIs are not path-symmetric.
Confirmed directly against GitHub's own spec: a repository is READ at `/repos/{owner}/{repo}` but
CREATED at `/orgs/{org}/repos` or `/user/repos` -- `/repos` alone doesn't exist as a collection path at
all. The reliable, real, cross-API pairing key `resourcemap.Discover` uses instead is response-schema
identity (matching the read and create operations' own `$ref` component name), not path structure --
path structure is only trusted for the narrower, reliably-real question "does this exact item path also
have a PATCH/PUT/DELETE." A second real finding from live validation: two distinct GitHub item paths
can legitimately share one response schema on purpose (`/gists/{gist_id}` and
`/gists/{gist_id}/{sha}`, both `gist-simple`) -- resolved as a deterministic skip-with-Note (shorter/
more-canonical path wins the name) rather than a hard error, so one such collision doesn't block every
other resource in the same document.

**Live validation, real proof, both real specs currently fetched from their real, official sources**:
GitHub (`github/rest-api-description`, `api.github.com.json`, ~12.9MB) -> **61 real resources
discovered** (`github_full_repository`, `github_issue`, `github_gist_simple`, `github_commit`, ...),
219 Notes. Datadog (`DataDog/datadog-api-client-go`'s own generator schema, v1 OpenAPI, ~1.6MB) -> **25
real resources discovered** (`datadog_dashboard`, `datadog_monitor`, `datadog_logs_pipeline`, ...), 471
Notes -- including `datadog_dashboard`'s own `widgets[].definition` field, a real `oneOf` of 41
structurally distinct branches, correctly and honestly typed as fully dynamic. Both runs gated behind
`UBX_LIVE_VALIDATION=1` (hermetic by default, matching this repo's own "`go test ./...` stays
hermetic" discipline). A separate, real end-to-end test (`TestServer_FullCRUDLifecycle`) drives a full
create/read/update/destroy cycle through the real `tfprotov6.ProviderServer` interface (real
`DynamicValue`/msgpack encoding, no transport mocking) against a real `net/http/httptest` server --
this is what caught a second real bug (a create-only path attribute like GitHub's own "org" was
silently nulled on every subsequent Read; fixed by widening `ReadResource`'s own carry-forward set to
include create-path params, not just read-path ones) before it could reach the live-spec validation at
all.

**Full repo `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` clean.** Never self-merged (nothing to merge -- no
remote exists yet for this new repo). No em dashes.

**Explicitly not done this phase, per its own scope**: auth implementations (config layer stubs the
interface only), async/retry execution semantics, drift rules, Smithy, the conformance gate. A real,
known gap surfaced but not solved: `ImportResourceState` can't recover a create-only path attribute
(no prior state to carry it from, and the read response never mentions it either) -- documented in
`Server.ImportResourceState`'s own comment, affects only resources whose Create and Read paths don't
share every param.

**Next steps for the founder's own checkpoint review**: whether to create a real GitHub remote for
`ubx-provider-dynamic` now or later; Phase 2 (auth implementations, real `[dynamic_providers.<name>.auth]`
types) is the natural next slice per the original 5-phase structure.

## UBI-172: mint dev "Client not built" -- root cause found, NOT fixable in this sandbox, state PR #15 OPEN not yet merged (never self-merged), 2026-08-15

**Do not re-investigate this from scratch.** The root cause is confirmed and the remedy is outside
this container. A one-line re-check is at the end.

### Root cause, verified end to end

`mint dev` does not build anything. It needs a **prebuilt Next.js standalone bundle** that the CLI
**downloads** from `https://releases.mintlify.com`. That host is **denied by the organization's
network egress policy**, so the bundle is never fetched and the renderer never exists.

The full chain, each step confirmed by running it:

1. `releases.mintlify.com` is blocked **both ways**. Through the agent proxy: `403` on
   `CONNECT releases.mintlify.com:443`, recorded in the proxy's own `recentRelayFailures` as
   `connect_rejected`, "gateway answered 403 (policy denial)". Bypassing the proxy: TLS completes
   against a transparent interceptor that returns **HTTP 403** with the body
   `Host not in allowlist: releases.mintlify.com. Add this host to your network egress settings to
   allow access.` Same policy, two expressions of it.
2. `getLatestClientVersion()` wraps that fetch in a `catch` that returns `undefined`. Verified by
   calling it directly: `getLatestClientVersion() => undefined`, `getClientVersion() => "none"`.
3. `mint update`'s client block is `if (latestClientVersion) { ... }`. With `undefined` it is
   skipped **silently** and the CLI prints **`success already up to date`** while no client is
   installed at all. That false success is why this never looked like a network problem.
4. `mint dev` never bootstraps the client anyway: `start.js` -> `dev()` -> `run.js` -> `setupNext()`
   with no download step in that path.
5. `setupNext()` hits ENOENT on
   `~/.mintlify/mint/apps/client/.next/required-server-files.json` and throws
   **"Client not built. Run: cd <path>/apps/client && STANDALONE_BUILD=true NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV=cli
   yarn build"**. That message is aimed at Mintlify's own monorepo developers, not at CLI users.
   **It is what misled four sessions into hunting for a missing local build step that does not
   exist for CLI installs.**

On disk: `~/.mintlify/mint/apps/client/` has `public/` and `src/` but **no** `.next/`, no
`mint-version.txt`, no `node_modules/next`.

### Not fixable here, and why

The allowlist is enforced upstream. The proxy reports `selective: false`, `toolScoped: false`, has
no writable allowlist endpoint (`POST /__agentproxy/allow` -> 405), and no egress config exists in
the repo or session settings. `/root/.ccr/README.md` is explicit for this failure class: a 403 is an
organization egress policy denial, and the instruction is to **report the blocked host, not retry or
route around it**. No fix was attempted or faked.

There is also no legitimate alternate source: the client bundle is **not** published on npm
(`@mintlify/client`, `mint-client`, `@mintlify/mint` are all unpublished; only the CLI tooling is),
and the CLI hardcodes `releases.mintlify.com` in `constants.js` with no mirror or local-bundle
override.

### What this is NOT

**Not a bug in the ubiquex-docs site.** `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` both pass here, on
every session, because neither needs the client bundle. The failure is entirely in fetching
Mintlify's prebuilt renderer.

**Not something a normal machine hits.** Any environment whose egress permits
`releases.mintlify.com` (an ordinary local dev machine, or this container with the host
allowlisted) runs `mint dev` fine. This is environment-specific, full stop.

### What future sessions should do

Expect the same limitation **unless the host gets allowlisted**. Keep using the measured
source-level substitute for DOM overflow checks and structural verification for redirects, and keep
saying plainly that the rendered check was not performed.

Cheap re-check, seconds, before assuming it is still blocked:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://releases.mintlify.com/mint-version.txt
```

`403` means still blocked. `200` means the allowlist changed: run `npx mint@latest update`, confirm
`~/.mintlify/mint/apps/client/.next/` now exists, and the real `mint dev` DOM and live-redirect
checks become available for the first time.

**The one action that would fix it** is adding `releases.mintlify.com` to this environment's network
egress allowlist, which is a Claude Code environment setting, not a repository change.

### Two real Mintlify CLI bugs found along the way

Neither is ours to fix, both worth knowing: `mint update` reports success when it silently skipped
the download, and `mint dev` reports a monorepo build instruction to CLI users whose actual problem
is a failed download. Either one alone would have made this a five-minute diagnosis instead of four
sessions of guessing.
